title: El juicio
summary: A minor property dispute in a small-town courtroom reveals a decades-old neighborhood secret during cross-examination that no one expected.

sentences.text: La sala del juzgado olía a madera vieja y a papeles acumulados durante décadas. El reloj de pared marcaba las diez y media y el termostato funcionaba mal, como siempre.
sentences.translation: The courtroom smelled of old wood and papers accumulated over decades. The wall clock read ten thirty and the thermostat was malfunctioning, as always.

sentences.text: La abogada joven, Andrea, colocó sus papeles sobre la mesa y respiró hondo. Su cliente, un señor mayor llamado don Emilio, la miraba con confianza. La demanda parecía sencilla: un límite de finca mal medido.
sentences.translation: The young lawyer, Andrea, placed her papers on the table and took a deep breath. Her client, an elderly man named Don Emilio, looked at her with confidence. The lawsuit seemed simple: a poorly measured property boundary.

sentences.text: El juez, un hombre canoso de gesto serio, dio inicio al juicio con un golpe seco de martillo. «Señoría, si me permite», comenzó Andrea, «me gustaría exponer los hechos de forma cronológica».
sentences.translation: The judge, a grey-haired man with a serious expression, began the trial with a sharp bang of the gavel. 'Your Honor, if you'll allow me,' Andrea began, 'I would like to present the facts chronologically.'

sentences.text: La parte contraria, representada por un abogado de la ciudad, insistía en que don Emilio había construido un muro que invadía la propiedad del demandante.
sentences.translation: The opposing party, represented by a city lawyer, insisted that Don Emilio had built a wall that encroached on the plaintiff's property.

sentences.text: «Con todo respeto», respondió Andrea, «insisto en que mi cliente actuó de buena fe. El muro se levantó donde, según la escritura de 1952, siempre estuvo el límite».
sentences.translation: 'With all due respect,' Andrea replied, 'I insist that my client acted in good faith. The wall was built where, according to the 1952 deed, the boundary always was.'

sentences.text: El abogado contrario llamó al primer testigo: una vecina del barrio que vivía en el número 12 desde hacía más de cuarenta años.
sentences.translation: The opposing lawyer called the first witness: a neighbor from the neighborhood who had lived at number 12 for over forty years.

sentences.text: La mujer declaró que recordaba perfectamente el límite original porque, de niña, jugaba en ese terreno. Pero cuando el abogado le preguntó si estaba segura, ella dudó.
sentences.translation: The woman testified that she clearly remembered the original boundary because, as a child, she played on that land. But when the lawyer asked if she was sure, she hesitated.

sentences.text: Fue entonces, durante el interrogatorio, cuando la testigo mencionó algo que no estaba en el expediente: «Don Emilio no es el dueño original. La finca era de su hermano, pero hubo un acuerdo verbal que nunca se escribió».
sentences.translation: It was then, during cross-examination, that the witness mentioned something that wasn't in the file: 'Don Emilio isn't the original owner. The estate belonged to his brother, but there was a verbal agreement that was never written down.'

sentences.text: Andrea sintió que el suelo se movía bajo sus pies. Nadie le había hablado de un hermano. Miró a don Emilio, que tenía la mirada fija en la mesa y las manos temblorosas.
sentences.translation: Andrea felt the ground move beneath her feet. No one had told her about a brother. She looked at Don Emilio, who was staring fixedly at the table with trembling hands.

sentences.text: Andrea pidió un receso. En el pasillo, don Emilio confesó: «Mi hermano se fue a América en los años sesenta y me dejó la casa. Nunca hicimos papeles. Éramos familia».
sentences.translation: Andrea requested a recess. In the hallway, Don Emilio confessed: 'My brother went to America in the sixties and left me the house. We never did the paperwork. We were family.'

sentences.text: Andrea respiró hondo y volvió a la sala. Sabía que el caso ya no trataba de un muro, sino de algo más delicado: una promesa entre hermanos que el derecho no reconocía.
sentences.translation: Andrea took a deep breath and returned to the courtroom. She knew the case was no longer about a wall, but about something more delicate: a promise between brothers that the law didn't recognize.

sentences.text: Andrea decidió cambiar de estrategia. Ya no discutiría el límite del terreno; pediría al juez que considerara la posesión continuada durante más de cincuenta años como título suficiente.
sentences.translation: Andrea decided to change strategy. She would no longer argue the boundary; she would ask the judge to consider continuous possession for over fifty years as sufficient title.

sentences.text: El juez escuchó los argumentos, ajustó las gafas y guardó silencio durante un minuto que a Andrea le pareció una hora.
sentences.translation: The judge listened to the arguments, adjusted his glasses, and remained silent for a minute that felt like an hour to Andrea.

sentences.text: Al final, el juez dictó un fallo que sorprendió a ambos lados: reconoció el derecho de don Emilio, pero le ordenó pagar una indemnización simbólica al demandante por la falta de documentación.
sentences.translation: In the end, the judge issued a ruling that surprised both sides: he recognized Don Emilio's right but ordered him to pay a symbolic compensation to the plaintiff for the lack of documentation.

language_notes.title: Reported speech with 'declaró que', 'insistía en que', 'confesó que'
language_notes.explanation: In legal reported speech, present tense shifts to imperfect and preterite to pluperfect. 'Recordaba' (she remembered) and 'jugaba' (she played) report past habits from a further past perspective.
language_notes.example: La mujer declaró que recordaba perfectamente el límite original porque, de niña, jugaba en ese terreno.
language_notes.example_translation: The woman testified that she clearly remembered the original boundary because, as a child, she played on that land.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Reported speech shifts the original tense back one step.
variants: El acusado insistió en que nunca había visto el documento
La testigo confirmó que la puerta estaba cerrada
El abogado argumentó que el contrato no era válido

language_notes.title: Subjunctive after 'pedir que', 'insistir en que' (influence verbs)
language_notes.explanation: 'Pedir que' + subjunctive ('considerara') is standard for requests and proposals. The imperfect subjunctive ('-ara' ending) follows past-tense main verbs.
language_notes.example: Andrea pidió al juez que considerara la posesión continuada como título suficiente.
language_notes.example_translation: Andrea asked the judge to consider continuous possession as sufficient title.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Verbs of request, suggestion, or insistence trigger the subjunctive.
variants: El juez pidió que el abogado presentara pruebas
Insistió en que el testigo dijera la verdad
Solicitaron que se aplazara la audiencia

language_notes.title: Legal connectors: 'con todo respeto', 'según', 'no obstante'
language_notes.explanation: In formal Spanish, 'con todo respeto' softens disagreement, 'según' attributes authority to a source, and 'no obstante' marks a concession before a counterargument.
language_notes.example: Con todo respeto, insisto en que mi cliente actuó de buena fe.
language_notes.example_translation: With all due respect, I insist that my client acted in good faith.
language_notes.pattern_hint: These connectors frame disagreement politely in formal settings.
variants: Según la escritura de 1952, el límite estaba más al norte
No obstante, la parte contraria presentó un testigo nuevo
A mi juicio, el acuerdo verbal carece de validez legal

language_notes.title: Implicit tone: describing emotion through physical detail
language_notes.explanation: Instead of saying 'Don Emilio estaba nervioso,' the story shows his anxiety through his fixed gaze and trembling hands — a sophisticated narrative technique typical of B2-level writing.
language_notes.example: don Emilio, que tenía la mirada fija en la mesa y las manos temblorosas.
language_notes.example_translation: Don Emilio, who was staring fixedly at the table with trembling hands.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Show emotion through physical description instead of naming it.
variants: Tenía la voz entrecortada y los ojos vidriosos
Tenía las manos firmes pero la respiración acelerada
Tenía el rostro pálido y las manos sobre la mesa

comprehension_questions.prompt: What makes the lawsuit seem simple at first?
choices: It is about a poorly measured property boundary
comprehension_questions.explanation: The story states 'La demanda parecía sencilla: un límite de finca mal medido' — a simple boundary dispute.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What unexpected information does the witness reveal during cross-examination?
choices: That the wall was built illegally
That Don Emilio has a brother who was the original owner with a verbal agreement
That the judge was involved in the original sale
comprehension_questions.explanation: The witness mentions Don Emilio is not the original owner — his brother was, with an unwritten verbal agreement: 'un acuerdo verbal que nunca se escribió.'

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why does Andrea change her legal strategy?
choices: She realizes the case is about an oral promise, not just a wall boundary
She decides to withdraw from the case
She wants to delay the proceedings
comprehension_questions.explanation: Andrea realizes 'el caso ya no trataba de un muro, sino de algo más delicado: una promesa entre hermanos' and shifts to arguing 'posesión continuada' instead.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What is the judge's final ruling?
choices: He rules entirely against Don Emilio
He recognizes Don Emilio's right but orders symbolic compensation
comprehension_questions.explanation: The judge issues a split ruling: 'reconoció el derecho de don Emilio, pero le ordenó pagar una indemnización simbólica al demandante por la falta de documentación.'

comprehension_questions.prompt: Which grammatical structure is used in 'Andrea insistió en que su cliente actuó de buena fe' that signals formal legal discourse?
choices: Preterite indicative after 'insistir en que' for a factual claim
comprehension_questions.explanation: 'Insistir en que' is followed by the indicative ('actuó') because Andrea is asserting a fact, not expressing doubt. In legal Spanish, this choice of mood carries evidentiary weight.

sentence_building.answer: La abogada joven, Andrea, colocó sus papeles sobre la mesa y respiró hondo. Su cliente, un señor mayor llamado don Emilio, la miraba con confianza. La demanda parecía sencilla: un límite de finca mal medido.
sentence_building.translation: The young lawyer, Andrea, placed her papers on the table and took a deep breath. Her client, an elderly man named Don Emilio, looked at her with confidence. The lawsuit seemed simple: a poorly measured property boundary.

sentence_building.answer: El juez escuchó los argumentos, ajustó las gafas y guardó silencio durante un minuto que a Andrea le pareció una hora.
sentence_building.translation: The judge listened to the arguments, adjusted his glasses, and remained silent for a minute that felt like an hour to Andrea.

title: El mercado de artesanos
summary: A visitor at an Oaxaca artisan market discovers that a seemingly simple ceramic piece carries a story her local guide won't translate.

sentences.text: El mercado de artesanos de Oaxaca bulle los sábados por la mañana. Clara, una turista inglesa, recorría los puestos con Pablo, un guía local que conocía cada rincón del mercado.
sentences.translation: The Oaxaca artisan market buzzes on Saturday mornings. Clara, an English tourist, was walking through the stalls with Pablo, a local guide who knew every corner of the market.

sentences.text: Pablo señalaba los textiles, las máscaras de madera y las piezas de barro mientras explicaba el origen de cada pieza con una seguridad que Clara admiraba.
sentences.translation: Pablo pointed out the textiles, the wooden masks, and the clay pieces while explaining the origin of each piece with a confidence that Clara admired.

sentences.text: En un puesto del fondo, un artesano zapoteca ordenaba piezas de barro pintadas a mano con formas de animales y flores. Clara se detuvo frente a una figura pequeña: un jaguar con manchas azules.
sentences.translation: At a stall at the back, a Zapotec artisan was arranging hand-painted clay pieces shaped like animals and flowers. Clara stopped in front of a small figure: a jaguar with blue spots.

sentences.text: —¿Cuánto cuesta? —preguntó Clara en su español titubeante. El artesano sonrió y dijo un precio. Pablo intervino: «Dice que trescientos pesos. Un poco caro, pero es auténtico».
sentences.translation: 'How much does it cost?' Clara asked in her halting Spanish. The artisan smiled and said a price. Pablo interjected: 'He says three hundred pesos. A bit expensive, but it's authentic.'

sentences.text: Clara no sabía si era caro o barato. Le gustaba la figura, pero algo en la mirada del artesano la hizo sentir que aquella pieza no era un simple recuerdo de viaje.
sentences.translation: Clara didn't know if it was expensive or cheap. She liked the figure, but something in the artisan's gaze made her feel that this piece wasn't a simple travel souvenir.

sentences.text: El artesano empezó a hablar en español, pero a media frase cambió a su lengua materna y dijo algo que Clara no entendió. Pablo frunció el ceño y no tradujo.
sentences.translation: The artisan started speaking in Spanish, but mid-sentence he switched to his mother tongue and said something Clara didn't understand. Pablo frowned and didn't translate.

sentences.text: —¿Qué ha dicho? —preguntó Clara. Pablo dudó. «No es importante. Cosas del taller. ¿Quieres regatear o lo pagas?»
sentences.translation: 'What did he say?' Clara asked. Pablo hesitated. 'It's not important. Workshop things. Do you want to haggle or pay the price?'

sentences.text: Clara intuyó que Pablo evitaba algo. Pagó los trescientos pesos, pero en lugar de irse, se quedó mirando la pieza. «¿Por qué hizo ese jaguar?», preguntó directamente al artesano.
sentences.translation: Clara sensed that Pablo was avoiding something. She paid the three hundred pesos, but instead of leaving, she stayed looking at the piece. 'Why did you make this jaguar?' she asked the artisan directly.

sentences.text: El artesano la miró a los ojos. Entonces, con gestos y palabras sueltas, le contó una historia que Clara entendió a medias: el jaguar era el guardián de un manantial que su abuelo había protegido hasta que llegaron las carreteras.
sentences.translation: The artisan looked her in the eyes. Then, with gestures and scattered words, he told her a story that Clara half-understood: the jaguar was the guardian of a spring that his grandfather had protected until the roads came.

sentences.text: Pablo escuchó en silencio. Cuando el artesano terminó, Pablo dijo: «Dice que el jaguar se quedó sin agua. Que la figura guarda la memoria del lugar donde él creció. No quise traducirlo porque no sabía si era para tanto».
sentences.translation: Pablo listened in silence. When the artisan finished, Pablo said: 'He says the jaguar was left without water. That the figure holds the memory of the place where he grew up. I didn't want to translate it because I didn't know if it was a big deal.'

sentences.text: Clara guardó la pieza con más cuidado que si fuera de cristal. No era un jaguar decorativo: era un testimonio de barro, la memoria de un lugar que ya no existía.
sentences.translation: Clara put the piece away more carefully than if it were made of glass. It wasn't a decorative jaguar: it was a clay testimony, the memory of a place that no longer existed.

sentences.text: Al salir del mercado, Clara dijo: «¿Sabes? Prefiero no haber entendido la traducción completa. Algunas historias se sienten mejor sin palabras exactas».
sentences.translation: Upon leaving the market, Clara said: 'You know? I prefer not having understood the full translation. Some stories feel better without exact words.'

example.text: El mercado de artesanos de Oaxaca bulle los sábados por la mañana.
example.translation: The Oaxaca artisan market buzzes on Saturday mornings.

example.text: piezas de barro pintadas a mano con formas de animales y flores.
example.translation: hand-painted clay pieces shaped like animals and flowers.

example.text: el artesano le contó algo en su lengua materna.
example.translation: the artisan told her something in his mother tongue.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: El artesano trabaja el barro desde niño.
La figura está hecha de barro.
Su lengua materna es el zapoteco.
El trueque sigue siendo común en las comunidades rurales.
El manantial alimenta todo el valle.
Su testimonio fue grabado en video.

language_notes.title: Imperfect for sensory description and ongoing states
language_notes.explanation: The imperfect ('señalaba', 'explicaba') creates a sensory snapshot of the market. It describes actions without a clear endpoint, anchoring the reader in the scene.
language_notes.example: Pablo señalaba los textiles, las máscaras de madera y las piezas de barro mientras explicaba el origen de cada pieza.
language_notes.example_translation: Pablo pointed out the textiles, the wooden masks, and the clay pieces while explaining the origin of each piece.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use imperfect for ongoing actions that set the scene.
variants: El vendedor mostraba las joyas mientras contaba su historia
Los turistas fotografiaban los puestos mientras el sol calentaba
La música sonaba de fondo mientras regateaban el precio

language_notes.title: Implicit stance: showing cultural judgment through silence
language_notes.explanation: Pablo's refusal to translate and his dismissive 'Cosas del taller' reveal his discomfort. The story trusts the reader to interpret this silence — a B2-level narrative technique.
language_notes.example: Pablo frunció el ceño y no tradujo. «No es importante. Cosas del taller.»
language_notes.example_translation: Pablo frowned and didn't translate. 'It's not important. Workshop things.'
language_notes.pattern_hint: A character's choice not to speak can convey more than dialogue.
variants: Miró hacia otro lado y dijo: 'No es nada'
Se encogió de hombros y cambió de tema
Hizo un gesto vago y respondió: 'Da igual'

language_notes.title: Subjunctive in relative clauses: 'un lugar que ya no existía' vs 'un lugar que no exista'
language_notes.explanation: The indicative 'existía' is used because the place's non-existence is a known fact. If the existence were uncertain ('buscaba un lugar que tuviera...'), the subjunctive would be required.
language_notes.example: No era un jaguar decorativo: era la memoria de un lugar que ya no existía.
language_notes.example_translation: It wasn't a decorative jaguar: it was the memory of a place that no longer existed.
language_notes.pattern_hint: When the existence of the place is known to be false, use indicative, not subjunctive.
variants: Buscaba un lugar que tuviera agua (subjunctive — unknown if it exists)
Recordaba un lugar que ya no existía (indicative — known to be gone)
Quería un jaguar que representara su historia (subjunctive — desired quality)

language_notes.title: Abstract nouns as narrative devices: 'memoria', 'testimonio', 'cosmovisión'
language_notes.explanation: B2-level Spanish uses abstract nouns ('memoria', 'testimonio') to layer meaning onto concrete objects, transforming a clay figure from a souvenir into a cultural artifact.
language_notes.example: era la memoria de un lugar que ya no existía.
language_notes.example_translation: it was the memory of a place that no longer existed.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Abstract nouns add interpretive depth to physical objects.
variants: El tejido era la crónica de una comunidad entera
La máscara era el eco de una ceremonia antigua
La canción era el reflejo de una infancia en el campo

comprehension_questions.prompt: What does Clara notice about the artisan when she asks about the jaguar piece?
choices: His gaze suggests the piece is more than a souvenir
He demands a much higher price
comprehension_questions.explanation: Clara senses 'algo en la mirada del artesano la hizo sentir que aquella pieza no era un simple recuerdo de viaje' — there is implicit meaning the piece carries.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why doesn't Pablo translate what the artisan says in his mother tongue?
choices: He didn't know if it was important enough to translate
He was angry at the artisan
comprehension_questions.explanation: Pablo admits 'no quise traducirlo porque no sabía si era para tanto' — he didn't judge the story as worth translating, revealing a cultural filter.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What story does the jaguar figure represent?
choices: The guardian of a spring that disappeared when roads were built
A hunting trophy from the jungle
comprehension_questions.explanation: The jaguar was 'el guardián de un manantial que su abuelo había protegido hasta que llegaron las carreteras' — a symbol of environmental loss.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What does Clara conclude about the experience at the end?
choices: She regrets not learning Zapotec before traveling
She prefers not having understood the full translation, as some stories feel better without exact words
She will only buy from tourist shops in the future
comprehension_questions.explanation: Clara says 'Prefiero no haber entendido la traducción completa. Algunas historias se sienten mejor sin palabras exactas' — embracing the ambiguity.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Which grammatical feature of the phrase 'guardaba la memoria del lugar donde él creció' makes it higher-level Spanish?
choices: The use of the conditional perfect
The imperfect 'guardaba' for a state that persists and 'donde' with preterite 'creció'
comprehension_questions.explanation: The imperfect 'guardaba' describes an ongoing quality (the figure holds memory), while 'donde él creció' uses preterite for a completed past action — a B2-level tense contrast.

sentence_building.answer: Pablo señalaba los textiles, las máscaras de madera y las piezas de barro mientras explicaba el origen de cada pieza con una seguridad que Clara admiraba.
sentence_building.translation: Pablo pointed out the textiles, the wooden masks, and the clay pieces while explaining the origin of each piece with a confidence that Clara admired.

sentence_building.answer: Clara guardó la pieza con más cuidado que si fuera de cristal. No era un jaguar decorativo: era un testimonio de barro, la memoria de un lugar que ya no existía.
sentence_building.translation: Clara put the piece away more carefully than if it were made of glass. It wasn't a decorative jaguar: it was a clay testimony, the memory of a place that no longer existed.

title: El vuelo reprogramado
summary: At Madrid Atocha, Pablo learns his flight to Lisbon was cancelled and must rebook by phone while the station loudspeakers never stop.

sentences.text: Pablo llegó a Atocha con la maleta pequeña y el abrigo a medio abrochar; el vestíbulo olía a café de máquina, a lluvia reciente y a anuncios que se solapaban en los altavoces.
sentences.translation: Pablo reached Atocha with a small suitcase and his coat half-buttoned; the concourse smelled of machine coffee and recent rain.

sentences.text: Abrió la app de la aerolínea: la pantalla parpadeó y cancelaron el vuelo de las diez por niebla en Lisboa.
sentences.translation: He opened the airline app: the screen flickered, and they cancelled the ten o’clock flight because of fog in Lisbon.

sentences.text: Los altavoces anunciaron retrasos en voz metálica; Pablo apretó el teléfono contra la oreja, miró el panel de salidas y esperó veinte minutos atrapado en la música de espera.
sentences.translation: The loudspeakers announced delays in a metallic voice; Pablo pressed the phone to his ear and waited twenty minutes to hold music.

sentences.text: «Solo quedan plazas en la reprogramación de mañana», dijo la agente, «o un tren nocturno con enlace al amanecer».
sentences.translation: “Only seats on tomorrow’s rescheduled flight remain,” said the agent, “or a night train with a connection at dawn.”

sentences.text: Pablo colgó, corrió al mostrador de la compañía y mostró el DNI entre dos viajeros que discutían por una maleta perdida.
sentences.translation: Pablo hung up, ran to the company counter, and showed his ID between two travellers arguing over a lost suitcase.

sentences.text: La empleada tecleó, suspiró y le entregó un código: «Tiene hasta las ocho para confirmar el tren en la app».
sentences.translation: The clerk typed, sighed, and handed him a code: “You have until eight to confirm the train in the app.”

sentences.text: Aceptó el enlace por la mañana, compró un bocadillo en la cafetería del andén y guardó el billete en el móvil.
sentences.translation: He accepted the morning connection, bought a sandwich at the platform café, and saved the ticket on his phone.

sentences.text: Cuando sonó la megafonía del andén 8, Pablo recogió la maleta y caminó entre turistas que miraban paneles interminables.
sentences.translation: When platform 8 was called over the PA, Pablo picked up his bag and walked among tourists staring at endless screens.

sentences.text: El tren entró con un frenazo suave; subió, encontró su asiento junto a la ventana empañada y respiró por primera vez en horas.
sentences.translation: The train rolled in with a gentle brake; he boarded, found his seat by the fogged window, and breathed properly for the first time in hours.

sentences.text: Mientras Madrid se alejaba por la vía hacia el sur, escribió a su hermana: «No volé, pero llego a Lisboa al mediodía; guarda el almuerzo y el billete nuevo».
sentences.translation: As Madrid fell away, he texted his sister: “I didn’t fly, but I’ll reach Lisbon by noon—save me lunch.”

example.text: Abrió la app de la aerolínea: la pantalla parpadeó y cancelaron el vuelo de las diez por niebla en Lisboa.

example.text: «Solo quedan plazas en la reprogramación de mañana»
example.translation: “Only seats on tomorrow’s rescheduled flight remain,” said the agent, “or a night train with a connection at dawn.”

Cancelaron el vuelo por la niebla.

language_notes.title: Describing things that just happened
language_notes.explanation: This pattern helps you describe an arrival and what you had with you.
language_notes.example: llegó a Atocha con la maleta pequeña y el abrigo a medio abrochar
language_notes.example_translation: (He) reached Atocha with a small suitcase and his coat half-buttoned
language_notes.pattern_hint: In Spanish, the preterite is typically used for finished actions.
variants: entró en la estación con el billete en mano y los nervios a flor de piel
salió de casa con el móvil apagado y la mochila lista
volvió al hotel con la lluvia en la chaqueta

language_notes.title: Reporting announcements or information
language_notes.explanation: Use this pattern for reporting announcements from people or devices.
language_notes.example: Los altavoces anunciaron retrasos en voz metálica
language_notes.example_translation: The loudspeakers announced delays in a metallic voice
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use this to say what something or someone announced.

language_notes.title: Offering limited choices
language_notes.explanation: This lets you tell someone what limited options are still available.
language_notes.example: Solo quedan plazas en la reprogramación de mañana
language_notes.example_translation: Only seats on tomorrow’s rescheduled flight remain
language_notes.pattern_hint: Solo quedan… means 'there are only...left.'
variants: solo quedan billetes en clase turista
solo quedan habitaciones para esta noche
solo quedan mesas cerca de la ventana

comprehension_questions.prompt: What happened to Pablo’s original flight?
choices: It was cancelled because of fog in Lisbon
He missed check-in at the airport
comprehension_questions.explanation: The airline app and the agent both cite fog in Lisbon («niebla en Lisboa») as the reason the flight was cancelled, not a simple delay.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why does Pablo go to Atocha instead of staying at the airport?
choices: He prefers the café on the platform
His new plan combines a train to Lisbon with a morning connection
He lost his passport at the station
comprehension_questions.explanation: The agent offers a night train plus a morning connection; Pablo accepts and heads to platform 8 with a new ticket on his phone.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Which detail shows preterite narration of completed events?
choices: «La pantalla parpadeó y cancelaron el vuelo de las diez»
«Los altavoces nunca dejan de anunciar retrasos»
comprehension_questions.explanation: «Parpadeó» and «cancelaron» are preterite: the screen blinked once, and the airline cancelled the flight—finished actions pushing the plot forward.

sentence_building.answer: Abrió la app de la aerolínea: la pantalla parpadeó y cancelaron el vuelo de las diez por niebla en Lisboa.
sentence_building.translation: He opened the airline app: the screen flickered, and they cancelled the ten o’clock flight because of fog in Lisbon.

sentence_building.answer: El tren entró con un frenazo suave; subió, encontró su asiento junto a la ventana empañada y respiró por primera vez en horas.
sentence_building.translation: The train rolled in with a gentle brake; he boarded, found his seat by the fogged window, and breathed properly for the first time in hours.

title: La entrevista final
summary: The final round interview at a Mexico City corporate headquarters takes a turn when the hiring manager asks a question that is not in the script.

sentences.text: Era la tercera entrevista en dos semanas. Valeria había pasado la prueba técnica, la conversación con recursos humanos y ahora, frente a ella, estaban el gerente de área y una mujer que no se había presentado.
sentences.translation: It was the third interview in two weeks. Valeria had passed the technical test, the HR conversation, and now, in front of her, were the area manager and a woman who had not introduced herself.

sentences.text: El gerente, un hombre de unos cincuenta años que se llamaba Arturo, comenzó con preguntas estándar: «Cuénteme sobre su experiencia liderando equipos. ¿Qué haría si un proyecto se retrasa?»
sentences.translation: The manager, a man about fifty named Arturo, started with standard questions: «Tell me about your experience leading teams. What would you do if a project is delayed?»

sentences.text: Valeria respondía con seguridad. Había ensayado cada respuesta con su hermana mayor y sabía que el tono era tan importante como el contenido. Pero la mujer silenciosa no dejaba de mirarla.
sentences.translation: Valeria answered confidently. She had rehearsed each answer with her older sister and knew that tone was as important as content. But the silent woman kept looking at her.

sentences.text: «¿Y si le pido que me describa un fracaso profesional, no una lección aprendida, sino un error real que todavía le duela?», preguntó la mujer. Arturo levantó una ceja; claramente esa pregunta no estaba en el guion.
sentences.translation: «And if I ask you to describe a professional failure, not a lesson learned, but a real mistake that still hurts?» the woman asked. Arturo raised an eyebrow; clearly that question was not in the script.

sentences.text: Valeria sintió que el suelo se abría. De repente, todas las respuestas preparadas dejaron de servir. Podía mentir o inventar un error menor, pero algo en la mirada de la mujer le dijo que detectaría la ficción.
sentences.translation: Valeria felt the floor open beneath her. Suddenly, all her prepared answers became useless. She could lie or invent a minor mistake, but something in the woman's gaze told her that the interviewer would detect the fiction.

sentences.text: Valeria respiró hondo y habló: «Hace dos años, lideré un proyecto de lanzamiento de producto en el que no escuché a mi equipo. Tenía prisa por cumplir el plazo y tomé decisiones unilaterales. El producto salió, pero dos personas renunciaron después».
sentences.translation: Valeria took a deep breath and spoke: «Two years ago, I led a product launch project where I did not listen to my team. I was in a hurry to meet the deadline and made unilateral decisions. The product launched, but two people quit afterward.»

sentences.text: Hubo un silencio. La mujer dejó de escribir. «¿Y qué aprendió?», preguntó. No era la típica pregunta de cierre; había un tono genuino de curiosidad.
sentences.translation: There was a silence. The woman stopped writing. «And what did you learn?» she asked. It was not the typical closing question; there was a genuine tone of curiosity.

sentences.text: «Aprendí», dijo Valeria, «que liderar no es solo tomar decisiones correctas, sino crear un espacio donde el equipo pueda decir que algo no va bien sin miedo. Aprendí que la confianza se gana escuchando, no dirigiendo».
sentences.translation: «I learned,» said Valeria, «that leading is not just about making the right decisions, but creating a space where the team can say something is not going well without fear. I learned that trust is earned by listening, not directing.»

sentences.text: Arturo asintió. La mujer cerró su cuaderno. «Gracias. Eso es exactamente lo que necesitaba oír. No la respuesta perfecta, sino la honestidad del error».
sentences.translation: Arturo nodded. The woman closed her notebook. «Thank you. That is exactly what I needed to hear. Not the perfect answer, but the honesty of the mistake.»

sentences.text: Valeria sonrió. No sabía si le ofrecerían el puesto, pero había algo más valioso: había dicho la verdad y, por primera vez en ese proceso, no se sintió como una candidata, sino como una persona.
sentences.translation: Valeria smiled. She did not know if they would offer her the position, but there was something more valuable: she had told the truth, and for the first time in that process, she did not feel like a candidate, but like a person.

sentences.text: Al salir, la mujer silenciosa la alcanzó en el ascensor. «No todo el mundo admite un error así. Vuelva mañana para hablar con el director general».
sentences.translation: As she was leaving, the silent woman caught up with her in the elevator. «Not everyone admits that kind of mistake. Come back tomorrow to speak with the CEO.»

sentences.text: Valeria no supo qué responder. A veces la puerta que parece cerrarse es la que se abre de verdad.
sentences.translation: Valeria did not know what to answer. Sometimes the door that seems to close is the one that truly opens.

example.text: Era la tercera entrevista en dos semanas.
example.translation: It was the third interview in two weeks.

language_notes.title: Reported speech across interview dialogue
language_notes.explanation: The story alternates between the narrator reported speech and direct interview quotes. This switch between registers is a key B2 narrative skill.
language_notes.example: El gerente comenzó con preguntas estándar: Cuénteme sobre su experiencia liderando equipos.
language_notes.example_translation: The manager started with standard questions: Tell me about your experience leading teams.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Direct quotes within reported narration mix formal and spoken registers.
variants: El director pregunto: Como manejaria un conflicto dentro del equipo?
La candidata respondio: Creo que la comunicacion temprana es clave.
El entrevistador dijo: Necesitamos a alguien que tome decisiones dificiles.

language_notes.title: Conditional for polite hypotheticals in interviews
language_notes.explanation: The conditional (haria, manejaria) is standard in professional Spanish for hypotheticals, creating polite distance between the speaker and the scenario.
language_notes.example: Que haria si un proyecto se retrasa?
language_notes.example_translation: What would you do if a project is delayed?
language_notes.pattern: Que [conditional verb] si [present or imperfect subjunctive]?
language_notes.pattern_hint: Interview questions use the conditional to soften hypothetical scenarios.
variants: Como manejaria una situacion de crisis?
Que cambios implementaria en el primer trimestre?
Que haria si un miembro del equipo no rinde?

language_notes.title: Mixed past tenses for narrative depth
language_notes.explanation: The pluperfect había pasado condenses earlier events into background, while the imperfect estaban places the reader in the current scene.
language_notes.example: Valeria había pasado la prueba técnica, la conversación con recursos humanos y ahora, frente a ella, estaban el gerente de área y una mujer.
language_notes.example_translation: Valeria had passed the technical test, the HR conversation, and now in front of her were the area manager and a woman.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Pluperfect summarizes completed prior events; imperfect sets the current scene.
variants: Habia investigado la empresa a fondo, pero la pregunta la tomo por sorpresa.
Habia dormido mal la noche anterior, pero se sentia concentrada.
Habia preparado cada respuesta, pero las palabras no salian.

language_notes.title: Abstract nouns in professional reflection
language_notes.explanation: B2 professional Spanish uses abstract nouns (confianza, honestidad) framed as general principles. The structure states universal truths with authority.
language_notes.example: la confianza se gana escuchando, no dirigiendo.
language_notes.example_translation: trust is earned by listening, not directing.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use abstract nouns as the subject of a general truth statement.
variants: El liderazgo se construye con ejemplo, no con autoridad.
La credibilidad se gana con resultados, no con promesas.
La colaboracion se fortalece compartiendo, no compitiendo.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What makes the silent woman question different from the others Valeria had been asked?
choices: It is a technical question about her field
It asks about a real failure that still hurts, not a rehearsed lesson-learned answer
comprehension_questions.explanation: The woman asks for a real mistake that still causes pain, which is deliberately outside the standard interview script.

comprehension_questions.prompt: How does Valeria respond to the unexpected question?

comprehension_questions.explanation: Valeria tells the truth about a failed product launch where she acted unilaterally to meet a deadline, causing two resignations.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What does Valeria say she learned from that failure?
choices: That deadlines should never be compromised

comprehension_questions.explanation: Valeria says leadership is not just making the right decisions but creating a space where the team can speak honestly without fear.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What does the observer say after Valeria honest answer?
choices: She looks disappointed and closes her notebook
She thanks Valeria for her honesty and invites her to speak with the CEO

comprehension_questions.prompt: What does Valeria realize at the end of the interview?
choices: She should have prepared better answers
Sometimes the door that seems to close is the one that truly opens

comprehension_questions.explanation: The narrator concludes that sometimes the door that appears to close is the one that truly opens, reflecting Valeria growth through vulnerability.

sentence_building.translation: The manager, a man about fifty named Arturo, started with standard questions: «Tell me about your experience leading teams. What would you do if a project is delayed?»

sentence_building.answer: Al salir, la mujer silenciosa la alcanzó en el ascensor. «No todo el mundo admite un error así. Vuelva mañana para hablar con el director general».
sentence_building.translation: As she was leaving, the silent woman caught up with her in the elevator. «Not everyone admits that kind of mistake. Come back tomorrow to speak with the CEO.»

title: La renuncia por correo
summary: After a bruising performance review, Marta drafts her resignation from a Barcelona office while voices still echo through the glass walls.

sentences.text: Era casi las siete cuando Marta entró en el despacho de la Diagonal; el aire olía a café recalentado, a tinta fresca de la impresora y a lluvia que golpeaba los ventanales.
sentences.translation: It was nearly seven when Marta stepped into her office on the Diagonal; the air smelled of reheated coffee, fresh printer ink, and rain tapping the glass walls.

sentences.text: La revisión del martes seguía abierta en la pantalla: comentarios en rojo que parecían más duros cada vez que los releía, como si alguien hubiera escrito el veredicto antes de escucharla.
sentences.translation: Tuesday’s review was still open on her screen—red comments that seemed harsher every time she read them again.

sentences.text: Mientras cerraba la puerta de cristal, oía a su jefe alzar la voz en la sala contigua; detrás, alguien reía con nerviosismo, como si el pasillo fuera un altavoz.
sentences.translation: As she shut the glass door, she could hear her boss raising his voice in the next room; behind that, someone laughed nervously, as if the hallway were a loudspeaker.

sentences.text: Abrió el portátil y escribió el asunto: «Renuncia voluntaria», con manos que ya no temblaban del todo.
sentences.translation: She opened her laptop and typed the subject line: “Voluntary resignation,” with hands that no longer trembled quite so much.

sentences.text: «Quería agradecer el tiempo en el equipo», escribía, aunque lo que deseaba era no volver a repetir aquella reunión.
sentences.translation: “I wanted to thank you for my time on the team,” she wrote, even though what she wanted was never to sit through that meeting again.

sentences.text: «Ojalá hubiera podido hablar antes de que tomaran la decisión», añadió, probando un subjuntivo que sonaba a carta antigua.
sentences.translation: “I wish I could have spoken before you made the decision,” she added, testing a subjunctive that sounded like an old-fashioned letter.

sentences.text: Releyó cada frase: si enviaba el correo, mañana ya no tendría llave del parking ni credencial azul.
sentences.translation: She read every sentence again: if she sent the email, tomorrow she would no longer have the parking pass or the blue badge.

sentences.text: Fuera, la Diagonal brillaba bajo una lluvia fina de mayo; dentro, el ascensor subía con un zumbido cansado que mezclaba voces y anuncios lejanos.
sentences.translation: Outside, the Diagonal gleamed under a fine May rain; inside, the lift climbed with a tired hum that blended voices and distant announcements.

sentences.text: Apretó «enviar» cuando el reloj marcaba las seis; el servidor tardó un segundo eterno en confirmarlo, y el borrador quedó vacío con la firma automática todavía pegada al pie.
sentences.translation: She hit “send” as the clock struck six; the server took an endless second to confirm it.

sentences.text: Guardó el portátil en la mochila, respiró hondo y salió sin esperar respuesta, como quien cierra un capítulo sin epílogo ni despedida en el ascensor.
sentences.translation: She slid the laptop into her backpack, drew a deep breath, and left without waiting for a reply—like someone closing a chapter with no epilogue and no goodbye in the lift.

language_notes.title: Talking about ongoing actions in the past
language_notes.explanation: Use this structure to describe two things happening at once in the past.
language_notes.example: Mientras cerraba la puerta de cristal, oía a su jefe alzar la voz
language_notes.example_translation: As she shut the glass door, she could hear her boss raising his voice
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'mientras' with the imperfect for actions happening at the same time in the past.
variants: Mientras escribía el correo, pensaba en la reunión
Mientras llovía fuera, Marta leía los comentarios

language_notes.title: Wishing things were different (I wish...)
language_notes.explanation: This pattern shows regret or unreal wishes for things that didn't happen.
language_notes.example: Ojalá hubiera podido hablar antes de que tomaran la decisión
language_notes.example_translation: I wish I could have spoken before you made the decision
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'ojalá' with the past subjunctive to express an unreal wish about the past.
variants: Ojalá no hubiera leído esos comentarios

language_notes.title: Describing how things seemed, felt, or looked (imperfect tense)
language_notes.explanation: Use the imperfect tense to set the background scene or describe an ongoing feeling in the past.
language_notes.example: el aire olía a café recalentado, a tinta fresca de la impresora y a lluvia
language_notes.example_translation: the air smelled of reheated coffee, fresh printer ink, and rain
language_notes.pattern_hint: The imperfect is often used for background descriptions in stories.
variants: El ascensor subía con un zumbido cansado

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why does Marta write the email that evening?
choices: She wants a promotion before the holidays
She is responding to a tense review and overheard criticism
Her laptop stopped working during the morning meeting
comprehension_questions.explanation: The review comments are still on her screen, and she hears her boss raising his voice next door—she decides to resign rather than repeat that meeting.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What does Marta lose if she sends the message?
choices: Her parking pass and blue company badge
Her train ticket home to Valencia
comprehension_questions.explanation: She re-reads the consequences: «mañana ya no tendría llave del parking ni credencial azul»—tomorrow she would no longer have the parking key or the blue badge.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Which line shows formal regret with the subjunctive?
choices: «Ojalá hubiera podido hablar antes de que tomaran la decisión»
«El ascensor subía con un zumbido cansado»
«La Diagonal brillaba bajo una lluvia fina de mayo»
comprehension_questions.explanation: «Ojalá hubiera podido…» uses the pluperfect subjunctive for a past wish, and «antes de que tomaran» triggers imperfect subjunctive after «antes de que»—typical of careful resignation register in Spain.

sentence_building.answer: La revisión del martes seguía abierta en la pantalla: comentarios en rojo que parecían más duros cada vez que los releía, como si alguien hubiera escrito el veredicto antes de escucharla.
sentence_building.translation: Tuesday’s review was still open on her screen—red comments that seemed harsher every time she read them again.

sentence_building.answer: Apretó «enviar» cuando el reloj marcaba las seis; el servidor tardó un segundo eterno en confirmarlo, y el borrador quedó vacío con la firma automática todavía pegada al pie.
sentence_building.translation: She hit “send” as the clock struck six; the server took an endless second to confirm it.

title: Le fromager du quartier
summary: Noah follows the aroma of cheese, tastes a nutty slice, and learns to wrap cheese like a local.

sentences.text: Noah entre dans la petite fromagerie quand l'odeur de fromage fondu lui chatouille le nez.
sentences.translation: Noah steps into the cozy cheese shop as the scent of melted cheese tickles his nose.

sentences.text: Le fromager porte un tablier blanc immaculé et dit bonjour avec un sourire chaleureux.
sentences.translation: The cheesemaker wears a pristine white apron and greets him with a warm smile.

sentences.text: Noah demande une tranche de fromage à pâte ferme avec des noisettes grillées.
sentences.translation: Noah asks for a slice of firm cheese with roasted hazelnuts.

sentences.text: Le fromager coupe la tranche doucement et enveloppe le morceau dans un papier craquant.
sentences.translation: The cheesemaker gently slices the cheese and wraps it in crinkly paper.

sentences.text: Noah paie avec des pièces brillantes et prend aussi un petit pain croustillant.
sentences.translation: Noah pays with shiny coins and also takes a crispy roll.

sentences.text: Il remercie encore et sort avec un sac léger. Le fromager lui rappelle de garder le fromage au frais jusqu'au dîner.
sentences.translation: He thanks the cheesemaker again and leaves with a light bag. The cheesemaker reminds him to keep the cheese cool until dinner.

title: Le pique-nique au parc
summary: Two friends share a simple Sunday picnic in a Paris park and learn that politeness shapes how food is offered and received in French.

sentences.text: Léa et Camille préparent un pique-nique pour leur dimanche au parc. Elles prennent du pain, du fromage et des fruits.
sentences.translation: Léa and Camille prepare a picnic for their Sunday at the park. They take bread, cheese, and fruit.

sentences.text: Au parc, le soleil brille et les oiseaux chantent. Elles mettent une nappe à carreaux rouges sur l'herbe verte.
sentences.translation: At the park, the sun shines and the birds sing. They put a red-checkered tablecloth on the green grass.

sentences.text: Léa sort le fromage et le pain. « Tu veux du fromage ? » demande-t-elle à Camille.
sentences.translation: Léa takes out the cheese and bread. "Do you want some cheese?" she asks Camille.

sentences.text: « Oui, merci ! » répond Camille. Elle prend une petite tranche. « C'est délicieux ! »
sentences.translation: "Yes, thank you!" replies Camille. She takes a small slice. "It's delicious!"

sentences.text: Léa coupe une part de gâteau et la donne à Camille. « C'est pour toi. »
sentences.translation: Léa cuts a slice of cake and gives it to Camille. "This is for you."

sentences.text: Camille dit : « Passe-moi la bouteille, s'il te plaît. » Léa lui donne l'eau fraîche.
sentences.translation: Camille says: "Pass me the bottle, please." Léa gives her the cold water.

sentences.text: Après le repas, elles ramassent tout et jettent les déchets dans une poubelle. « Il faut être propre », dit Léa.
sentences.translation: After the meal, they pick everything up and throw the trash in a bin. "We must be clean," says Léa.

sentences.text: Elles marchent ensemble vers la sortie du parc. Camille sourit. « C'était un très bon dimanche. »
sentences.translation: They walk together toward the park exit. Camille smiles. "It was a very good Sunday."

title: Une promenade le long de la Seine
summary: Lucas follows the Seine past bouquiniste boxes and a quiet bateau-mouche before finding a bench beneath the trees.

sentences.text: C'est un dimanche après-midi paisible. Le ciel est d'un bleu éclatant et l'air est doux.
sentences.translation: It's a peaceful Sunday afternoon. The sky is a brilliant blue and the air is mild.

sentences.text: Lucas décide de se promener le long de la Seine. L'eau de la rivière est calme et d'un vert profond.
sentences.translation: Lucas decides to take a stroll along the Seine. The river water is calm and a deep green.

sentences.text: Sur les quais, des gens lisent des livres et des enfants rient.
sentences.translation: On the riverbanks, people read books and children laugh.

sentences.text: Lucas passe devant les boîtes des bouquinistes, pleines de trésors. Il admire les vieux livres et les cartes postales anciennes.
sentences.translation: Lucas walks past the booksellers' boxes, full of treasures. He admires the old books and vintage postcards.

sentences.text: Un bateau-mouche glisse sous le pont, silencieux. Les touristes capturent des souvenirs en photos.
sentences.translation: A tour boat glides silently under the bridge. Tourists capture memories in photos.

sentences.text: Lucas s'arrête près d'un arbre et s'assoit sur un banc.
sentences.translation: Lucas stops near a tree and sits on a bench.

sentences.text: Il contemple les nuages blancs qui flottent dans le ciel. Un petit oiseau chante doucement dans les branches.
sentences.translation: He gazes at the white clouds floating in the sky. A little bird sings softly in the branches.

sentences.text: « Paris est vraiment belle », pense Lucas avec émerveillement. Il reste là une heure, tranquille et heureux.
sentences.translation: "Paris is truly beautiful," Lucas thinks with wonder. He stays there for an hour, peaceful and happy.

title: Une rencontre au café
summary: Marie is sitting at the terrace of a café. She is drinking a coffee with cream and reading the newspaper.

sentences.text: Marie est assise à la terrasse d'un café animé. Elle boit un café crème parfumé et lit le journal.
sentences.translation: Marie is seated at the bustling terrace of a café. She sips a fragrant coffee with cream and reads the newspaper.

sentences.text: Un homme élégant arrive et demande : « Excusez-moi, cette place est libre ? »
sentences.translation: A well-dressed man arrives and asks, "Excuse me, is this seat free?"

sentences.text: « Oui, bien sûr », répond Marie avec un sourire.
sentences.translation: "Yes, of course," Marie replies with a smile.

sentences.text: L'homme s'assoit. Il s'appelle Thomas. Marie demande : « Que faites-vous dans la vie ? » « Je suis professeur de musique. »

title: Cinq minutes sous la pluie
summary: On a rainy Clichy bus, Nora must choose between helping with a stroller and arriving on time.

sentences.text: À 8 h 12, le bus 62 était déjà plein devant la mairie de Clichy. Il pleuvait, et l'intérieur du bus sentait les manteaux mouillés.
sentences.translation: At 8:12, the 62 bus was already packed in front of Clichy town hall. It was raining, and the inside of the bus smelled like wet coats.

sentences.text: Nora tenait son sac contre elle ; elle répétait dans sa tête la phrase pour son entretien : « Je travaillais à l'accueil. »
sentences.translation: Nora held her bag close; in her head, she kept repeating the line for her interview: “I worked at reception.”

sentences.text: Au troisième arrêt, une femme est montée avec une poussette, mais personne ne bougeait. Le chauffeur a attendu, les portes ouvertes.
sentences.translation: At the third stop, a woman got on with a stroller, but no one moved. The driver waited with the doors open.

sentences.text: Nora avait une place près de la fenêtre. Si elle restait assise, elle arriverait à l'heure ; si elle aidait, peut-être pas.
sentences.translation: Nora had a seat by the window. If she stayed seated, she would arrive on time; if she helped, maybe not.

sentences.text: Elle s'est levée et a souri : « Je vous aide ? » Ensemble, elles ont plié la poussette doucement, entre deux sacs.
sentences.translation: She stood up and smiled: “Can I help you?” Together, they folded the stroller carefully between two bags.

sentences.text: La femme l'a remerciée, un peu gênée. Le bus repartait quand Nora a vu son téléphone : un message du recruteur.
sentences.translation: The woman thanked her, a little embarrassed. The bus was pulling away when Nora saw her phone: a message from the recruiter.

sentences.text: « Cinq minutes de retard, pas de souci. » Nora a enfin respiré. Dehors, Clichy brillait sous la pluie, et le bus avançait.
sentences.translation: “Five minutes late is no problem.” Nora finally breathed again. Outside, Clichy shone in the rain, and the bus moved on.

title: Un dîner entre amis
summary: Julie invites Paul for a cozy dinner. Together, they create a delicious quiche, filling the kitchen with laughter and the aroma of melted cheese.

sentences.text: Ce soir, Julie invite son ami Paul à dîner. Ils décident de cuisiner ensemble.
sentences.translation: This evening, Julie invites her friend Paul for dinner. They decide to cook together.

sentences.text: « On prépare une quiche ? » propose Julie avec un sourire. « Excellente idée ! » répond Paul avec enthousiasme.
sentences.translation: “Shall we make a quiche?” Julie suggests with a smile. “Excellent idea!” Paul replies enthusiastically.

sentences.text: Julie coupe les oignons et les tomates, et leur parfum emplit la cuisine.
sentences.translation: Julie chops the onions and tomatoes, their aroma filling the kitchen.

sentences.text: Paul casse les œufs dans un bol et ajoute la crème, créant un mélange onctueux.
sentences.translation: Paul cracks the eggs into a bowl and adds the cream, creating a smooth mixture.

sentences.text: « Il nous faut aussi du fromage », dit Julie. Paul râpe rapidement le fromage.
sentences.translation: “We also need cheese,” Julie says. Paul quickly grates the cheese.

sentences.text: Ils mélangent tout et mettent la quiche au four. Elle cuit doucement.
sentences.translation: They mix everything and put the quiche in the oven. It cooks slowly.

sentences.text: En attendant, ils préparent une salade verte fraîche et croquante, assaisonnée d'une vinaigrette.
sentences.translation: While they wait, they prepare a fresh, crisp green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

sentences.text: Après trente minutes, la quiche est prête. Toute la cuisine sent bon.
sentences.translation: After thirty minutes, the quiche is ready. The whole kitchen smells wonderful.

sentences.text: Ils s'assoient à table et mangent ensemble. « C'est délicieux ! » s'exclame Paul.
sentences.translation: They sit at the table and eat together. “It’s delicious!” Paul exclaims.

sentences.text: « On cuisine bien ensemble », rit Julie. Ils finissent le repas avec un fondant au chocolat et du thé parfumé.
sentences.translation: “We cook well together,” Julie laughs. They finish the meal with a chocolate fondant and fragrant tea.

title: Un train pour Marseille
summary: A missed station announcement sends Inès to an attendant, where one clear question gets her journey to Marseille back on track.

sentences.text: Inès est arrivée à la gare avec une valise trop lourde et un café tiède à moitié bu.
sentences.translation: Inès arrived at the station with a suitcase too heavy and a lukewarm coffee half-drunk.

sentences.text: Elle n'a pas compris la première annonce, alors elle a demandé à une agente souriante : « Sur quel quai part le train pour Marseille ? »
sentences.translation: She didn't understand the first announcement, so she asked a smiling attendant, “Which platform does the train to Marseille leave from?”

sentences.text: L'écran indiquait dix minutes de retard, mais le quai restait le même.
sentences.translation: The screen showed a ten-minute delay, but the platform remained the same.

sentences.text: Pendant l'attente, Inès a vérifié sa correspondance et a noté le numéro du quai dans son carnet.
sentences.translation: While she waited, Inès checked her connection and noted the platform number in her notebook.

sentences.text: Pendant le trajet, elle regardait les oliviers et les petites maisons blanches qui défilaient rapidement.
sentences.translation: During the journey, she watched the olive trees and small white houses flash by.

sentences.text: À Marseille, elle a senti l'air plus chaud et vu la lumière se refléter sur les façades. Elle a souri : son voyage commençait enfin.
sentences.translation: In Marseille, she felt the warmer air and saw light reflecting on the buildings. She smiled: her trip was finally beginning.

title: Un week-end à Lyon
summary: Emma spends a weekend in Lyon and discovers the city through food, walking, and a small mistake.

sentences.text: Emma est arrivée à Lyon un samedi matin avec un petit sac et beaucoup de curiosité.
sentences.translation: Emma arrived in Lyon on a Saturday morning with a small bag and a lot of curiosity.

sentences.text: Elle voulait explorer la vieille ville, savourer un repas dans un bouchon et flâner le long de la Saône.
sentences.translation: She wanted to explore the old city, enjoy a meal in a traditional Lyon restaurant, and stroll along the Saône.

sentences.text: Après avoir déposé son sac à l'hôtel, elle a cherché une boulangerie pour acheter une brioche aux pralines roses.
sentences.translation: After leaving her bag at the hotel, she looked for a bakery to buy a pink-praline brioche.

sentences.text: Dans la rue, elle a pris le mauvais bus et s'est retrouvée loin du centre.
sentences.translation: On the street, she took the wrong bus and ended up far from the center.

sentences.text: Au lieu de paniquer, elle a demandé de l'aide à une femme à l'arrêt.
sentences.translation: Instead of panicking, she asked a woman at the stop for help.

sentences.text: La femme lui a expliqué le chemin avec beaucoup de patience. Finalement, Emma est arrivée dans le Vieux Lyon juste avant midi.
sentences.translation: The woman explained the route very patiently. Finally, Emma reached Old Lyon just before noon.

sentences.text: Elle était un peu fatiguée, mais elle avait déjà une histoire à raconter.
sentences.translation: She was a little tired, but she already had a story to tell.

title: Une surprise au bureau
summary: Nadia expects an ordinary workday, but her colleagues have prepared a warm surprise for her work anniversary.

title: Au marché
summary: Claire navigates a vibrant market, her senses alive with colors and sounds, as she fills her bag with fresh produce and flowers.

sentences.text: C'est samedi matin, et Claire se promène au marché avec son grand sac en osier. Le marché est un tourbillon de couleurs et de sons.
sentences.translation: It's Saturday morning, and Claire strolls through the market with her large wicker bag. The market is a whirlwind of colors and sounds.

sentences.text: Il y a des fruits rouges brillants, des légumes verts croquants et des fleurs jaunes éclatantes partout.
sentences.translation: There are bright red fruits, crisp green vegetables, and vibrant yellow flowers everywhere.

sentences.text: « Bonjour ! Je voudrais un kilo de pommes, s'il vous plaît », dit Claire au vendeur avec un sourire.
sentences.translation: “Hello! I would like a kilo of apples, please,” Claire says to the seller with a smile.

sentences.text: « Voilà, madame. Deux euros », répond-il en tendant le sac.
sentences.translation: “Here you are, ma’am. Two euros,” he replies, handing her the bag.

sentences.text: Claire achète aussi des carottes orange, un fromage blanc crémeux et six œufs frais.
sentences.translation: Claire also buys orange carrots, creamy white cheese, and six fresh eggs.

sentences.text: Elle s'arrête devant les fleurs, attirée par leur parfum doux. « Combien coûtent les tulipes ? » demande-t-elle.
sentences.translation: She stops in front of the flowers, drawn by their sweet scent. “How much are the tulips?” she asks.

sentences.text: « Cinq euros le bouquet », répond le vendeur. Claire choisit un bouquet de tulipes roses.
sentences.translation: “Five euros per bouquet,” the seller replies. Claire chooses a bouquet of pink tulips.

sentences.text: Son sac est lourd maintenant, mais elle est contente.
sentences.translation: Her bag is heavy now, but she is happy.

sentences.text: À la maison, elle met les fleurs dans un vase sur la table, illuminant la pièce.
sentences.translation: At home, she puts the flowers in a vase on the table, brightening the room.

title: La rencontre au marché
summary: Two strangers meet at a cheese stall in a Lyon market and discover they both want the last portion of Comté.

sentences.text: C'était samedi matin, et le marché de la Croix-Rousse battait son plein. Les étals débordaient de légumes colorés et d'épices odorantes.
sentences.translation: It was Saturday morning, and the Croix-Rousse market was in full swing. The stalls overflowed with colorful vegetables and fragrant spices.

sentences.text: Devant le stand de fromages, une dizaine de personnes attendaient leur tour. Chloé regardait la dernière portion de Comté avec envie.
sentences.translation: In front of the cheese stall, about ten people were waiting their turn. Chloé eyed the last portion of Comté eagerly.

sentences.text: « Il ne me reste qu'une portion de Comté », annonça le fromager.
sentences.translation: “I only have one portion of Comté left,” the cheesemonger announced.

sentences.text: Quand leur tour arriva, Chloé et un jeune homme — Hugo — demandèrent le Comté en même temps. Ils échangèrent un regard gêné.
sentences.translation: When their turn came, Chloé and a young man—Hugo—asked for the Comté at the same time. They exchanged an awkward look.

sentences.text: « Après vous, madame, » proposa Hugo poliment. Chloé hésita. « Non, vraiment, vous étiez là avant moi, je crois. »
sentences.translation: "After you, madam," Hugo offered politely. Chloé hesitated. "No, really, you were here before me, I think."

sentences.text: Finalement, Hugo fit un geste élégant et dit : « Je vous cède la place. Mais peut-être pourrions-nous partager la portion ? »
sentences.translation: Finally, Hugo made an elegant gesture and said, “I'll let you go first. But perhaps we could share the portion?”

sentences.text: Chloé sourit. « Partager ? C'est une idée qui me plaît. » Le fromager les regarda, amusé, et coupa la portion en deux.
sentences.translation: Chloé smiled. “Share? That's an idea I like.” The cheesemonger watched them, amused, and cut the portion in two.

sentences.text: Pendant qu'il emballait les parts, Hugo et Chloé se mirent à discuter. Il était architecte ; elle travaillait dans une librairie du Vieux Lyon.
sentences.translation: While he wrapped the portions, Hugo and Chloé started chatting. He was an architect; she worked in a bookshop in Old Lyon.

sentences.text: « Vous connaissez un bon endroit pour déguster du Comté avec un verre de vin ? » demanda Hugo. Chloé réfléchit une seconde.
sentences.translation: "Do you know a good place to taste Comté with a glass of wine?" asked Hugo. Chloé thought for a second.

sentences.text: « Oui, justement, le bistro en bas de ma rue. Si vous voulez, je vous montrerai. » Leur compétition s'était transformée en rendez-vous.
sentences.translation: "Yes, actually, the bistro at the bottom of my street. If you want, I'll show you." Their competition had turned into a date.

title: La réunion des anciens
summary: At a class reunion in Brittany, an old photograph forces former classmates to confront a silence they have carried for twenty years.

sentences.text: Dans un petit café de Bretagne, la réunion des anciens élèves battait son plein. On avait installé des guirlandes et sorti le cidre local.
sentences.translation: In a small café in Brittany, the former students' reunion was in full swing. They had hung garlands and brought out the local cider.

sentences.text: Une trentaine d'anciens camarades s'étaient retrouvés après vingt ans. Certains ne s'étaient pas vus depuis la remise des diplômes.
sentences.translation: About thirty former classmates had reunited after twenty years. Some hadn't seen each other since graduation day.

sentences.text: C'est en fouillant dans une boîte de souvenirs que Pierre sortit un vieux cliché jauni. Il le montra à la cantonade. « Vous vous souvenez de ce jour-là ? »
sentences.translation: It was while rummaging through a box of memories that Pierre pulled out an old yellowed photograph. He showed it to everyone. "Do you remember that day?"

sentences.text: Les visages s'illuminèrent. La photo montrait la classe devant le lycée, un jour de grève générale. Mais au second plan, une silhouette souriait d'un air mystérieux.
sentences.translation: Faces lit up. The photo showed the class in front of the school, on a day of a general strike. But in the background, a figure smiled mysteriously.

sentences.text: « Qui est cette personne ? » demanda Sophie en plissant les yeux. « Je ne l'ai jamais vue. » Un silence gêné s'installa autour de la table.
sentences.translation: "Who is this person?" asked Sophie, squinting. "I've never seen her." An awkward silence settled around the table.

sentences.text: « Ce cliché cache un secret, » murmura Pierre, le regard fixé sur l'image. Les regards se figèrent. Chacun regardait la photo en silence.
sentences.translation: "This photo hides a secret," Pierre murmured, his gaze fixed on the image. Looks froze. Everyone stared at the photo in silence.

sentences.text: Le café autour d'eux continuait à bourdonner, mais leur table était devenue une île. Personne ne voulait être le premier à dire ce qu'il savait ou devinait.
sentences.translation: The café around them kept buzzing, but their table had become an island. No one wanted to be the first to say what they knew or guessed.

sentences.text: « C'était Mme Le Goff, notre remplaçante », dit enfin Marcel. « Elle nous avait rejoints devant le lycée pour soutenir la grève. La direction l'a renvoyée le lendemain. »
sentences.translation: “It was Ms. Le Goff, our substitute teacher,” Marcel finally said. “She joined us outside the school to support the strike. The administration dismissed her the next day.”

sentences.text: Sophie reposa la photo sur la table. « Et nous n'avons rien dit pour la défendre », murmura-t-elle. Personne ne la contredit.
sentences.translation: Sophie put the photo back on the table. “And we said nothing to defend her,” she murmured. No one contradicted her.

sentences.text: Le patron du café apporta une tournée de kouign-amann. La conversation reprit, mais plus basse, comme si le poids des années non dites pesait sur leurs épaules.
sentences.translation: The café owner brought a round of kouign-amann. The conversation resumed, but lower, as if the weight of unspoken years pressed on their shoulders.

sentences.text: En partant, Pierre glissa la photo dans sa poche. Le lendemain, il chercherait Mme Le Goff. Certains souvenirs, comprit-il, ne demandent pas à rester enfouis, mais à être enfin racontés.
sentences.translation: As he left, Pierre slipped the photo into his pocket. The next day, he would look for Ms. Le Goff. Some memories, he understood, should not stay buried but finally be told.

title: Le musée Rodin en octobre
summary: Sara visits on a grey Tuesday, copies one line from a cartel beside Le Penseur, and leaves believing marble can still argue gently.

sentences.text: Sara avait réservé sa visite un mardi pluvieux parce qu'elle détestait faire la queue quand le soleil attirait trop de monde.
sentences.translation: Sara had booked her visit for a rainy Tuesday because she hated queuing when sunny days drew too many people.

sentences.text: Une bruine fine collait les feuilles mortes aux pavés près du mur du musée Rodin ; elle serrait un parapluie gris et un carnet flambant neuf.
sentences.translation: A fine drizzle glued fallen leaves to the cobblestones near the Rodin Museum wall; she clutched a grey umbrella and a brand-new notebook.

sentences.text: À l'intérieur, le marbre semblait encore tiède sous ses doigts effleurant une main sculptée, comme si les gestes anciens pouvaient réchauffer l'hiver avant même novembre.
sentences.translation: Inside, the marble felt almost warm under her fingers brushing a sculpted hand, as if ancient gestures could warm the winter before November even arrived.

sentences.text: Elle lisait lentement les cartels bilingues jusqu'à ce qu'elle trouve une phrase sur la patience du matériau—des mots modestes face au tumulte des visites pressées.
sentences.translation: She slowly read the bilingual plaques until she found a phrase about the patience of the material—modest words amidst the rush of hurried visits.

sentences.text: Dans le jardin humide, quelques enfants couraient autour du Penseur, mais elle s'est contentée de noter la phrase avant de fermer son carnet.
sentences.translation: In the damp garden, a few children ran around the Thinker, but she simply noted the phrase before closing her notebook.

sentences.text: En sortant, elle n'a acheté aucune carte postale : elle préférait garder trois images floues en mémoire plutôt qu'un fichier parfait.
sentences.translation: As she left, she bought no postcards: she preferred to keep three blurry images in her mind rather than a perfect file.

sentences.text: Elle est rentrée les pieds mouillés en pensant qu'à Paris certains monuments demandent encore le silence avant la photo finale.
sentences.translation: She returned home with wet feet, thinking that in Paris, some monuments still demand silence before the final photo.

sentences.text: Le soir, elle a relu la phrase et l'a répétée à voix haute. Sa visite continuait ainsi, dans le silence de sa chambre.
sentences.translation: That evening, she reread the sentence and repeated it aloud. In this way, her visit continued in the quiet of her room.
