title: Les voisins du dessous
summary: A noise complaint note stuck to the door in a Lyon apartment building leads two neighbors from tension to an unlikely friendship.

sentences.text: Depuis quelques semaines, un bruit de pas régulier perturbait le calme de l'immeuble. Marc, au premier étage, n'arrivait plus à lire le soir sans entendre des allées et venues.
sentences.translation: For a few weeks, a regular sound of footsteps had been disturbing the building's peace. Marc, on the first floor, could no longer read in the evening without hearing comings and goings.

sentences.text: Un matin, en sortant de chez elle, Chloé trouva un mot plié sous sa porte. « Vos pas sont très bruyants après vingt-deux heures. Merci de faire attention. »
sentences.translation: One morning, leaving her apartment, Chloé found a folded note under her door. "Your footsteps are very loud after ten p.m. Please be mindful."

sentences.text: Chloé lut le mot deux fois. D'abord, elle se sentit vexée. Ensuite, elle soupira. Il avait raison: elle dansait souvent dans son salon tard le soir.
sentences.translation: Chloé read the note twice. At first, she felt offended. Then she sighed. He was right: she often danced in her living room late at night.

sentences.text: Elle prit son courage à deux mains et monta s'excuser. « Désolée pour le bruit. Dans ma nouvelle colocation, je répète souvent mes chorégraphies le soir, mais je ferai attention. »
sentences.translation: She gathered her courage and went upstairs to apologize. “Sorry about the noise. In my new shared flat, I often rehearse my dance routines in the evening, but I'll be careful.”

sentences.text: Marc ouvrit la porte, surpris. Il s'attendait à une réponse agressive ou à du silence. « Ah, euh... merci. Moi non plus, je ne voulais pas être désagréable. »
sentences.translation: Marc opened the door, surprised. He had expected an aggressive response or silence. "Oh, uh... thank you. I didn't want to be unpleasant either."

sentences.text: Ils restèrent un moment sur le palier, un peu gênés. Puis Chloé remarqua les livres empilés près de sa porte. « Vous lisez beaucoup ? » demanda-t-elle.
sentences.translation: They stood on the landing for a moment, a little awkward. Then Chloé noticed the books stacked near his door. "Do you read a lot?" she asked.

sentences.text: Marc lui montra le roman qu'il était en train de finir. Chloé reconnut la couverture. « Je l'ai lu le mois dernier ! Vous voulez que je vous prête le suivant ? »
sentences.translation: Marc showed her the novel he was finishing. Chloé recognized the cover. "I read it last month! Do you want me to lend you the next one?"

sentences.text: Quelques jours plus tard, Chloé déposa le livre devant sa porte avec un petit mot: « Celui-ci est encore mieux. Bonne lecture ! »
sentences.translation: A few days later, Chloé left the book at his door with a little note: "This one is even better. Happy reading!"

sentences.text: Marc lui rendit le prêt avec une bouteille de vin et une invitation: « Si vous voulez, on peut en discuter autour d'un verre. »
sentences.translation: Marc returned the loan with a bottle of wine and an invitation: "If you want, we can discuss it over a glass."

sentences.text: Le bruit de pas n'avait pas complètement disparu. Mais désormais, au lieu d'un mot froid, c'était un SMS amical qui accompagnait les soirs de danse: « Désolée, je fais attention ! »
sentences.translation: The sound of footsteps hadn't completely disappeared. But now, instead of a cold note, a friendly text accompanied the dance nights: "Sorry, I'm being careful!"

example.text: Un matin, en sortant de chez elle, Chloé trouva un mot plié sous sa porte.
example.translation: One morning, leaving her apartment, Chloé found a folded note under her door.

example.text: Depuis quelques semaines, un bruit de pas régulier perturbait le calme de l'immeuble.
example.translation: For a few weeks, a regular sound of footsteps had been disturbing the building's peace.

example.text: « Désolée pour le bruit. C'est juste que ma nouvelle colocation est un peu bruyante. »
example.translation: "Sorry about the noise. It's just that my new shared flat is a bit loud."

example.text: Elle prit son courage à deux mains et monta s'excuser.
example.translation: She gathered her courage and went upstairs to apologize.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Le bruit des pas dérange tout l'immeuble.
Il faut savoir s'excuser quand on fait du bruit.
Ils se sont rencontrés sur le palier.

language_notes.title: Writing a polite complaint note
language_notes.explanation: In French apartment culture, 'Merci de + infinitive' is a standard way to make a request without sounding aggressive.
language_notes.example: Vos pas sont très bruyants après vingt-deux heures. Merci de faire attention.
language_notes.example_translation: Your footsteps are very loud after ten p.m. Please be mindful.
language_notes.pattern_hint: State the issue directly, then add a polite request.
variants: Votre musique est forte le soir. Merci de baisser le son.
La porte claque souvent. Merci de la fermer doucement.
L'odeur de cuisine monte. Merci d'aérer moins longtemps.

language_notes.title: Apologizing face-to-face
language_notes.explanation: A direct apology followed by a short explanation is the most effective way to defuse neighbor tension in French.
language_notes.example: Désolée pour le bruit. C'est juste que ma nouvelle colocation est un peu bruyante.
language_notes.example_translation: Sorry about the noise. It's just that my new shared flat is a bit loud.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Start with 'Désolé(e) pour' then explain without making excuses.
variants: Désolée pour le dérangement. C'est que j'ai des travaux.
Désolé pour l'odeur. Je viens de faire cuire du poisson.
Désolée pour l'attente. J'ai eu un imprévu.

language_notes.title: Softening a statement with 'un peu'
language_notes.explanation: At B1, using 'un peu' signals that you're aware of the issue without overstating it — a key social skill in French conversation.
language_notes.example: Ma nouvelle colocation est un peu bruyante.
language_notes.example_translation: My new shared flat is a bit loud.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Add 'un peu' before an adjective to soften criticism.
variants: Mon appartement est un peu petit.
Le quartier est un peu bruyant la nuit.
La cuisine est un peu sombre.

language_notes.title: Making an invitation after resolving a conflict
language_notes.explanation: This construction keeps the invitation casual and leaves the other person room to decline gracefully.
language_notes.example: Si vous voulez, on peut en discuter autour d'un verre.
language_notes.example_translation: If you want, we can discuss it over a glass.
language_notes.pattern: Si vous voulez, on peut [verb] [optional detail]
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'Si vous voulez' to make an open, non-pushy invitation.
variants: Si vous voulez, on peut boire un café.
Si tu veux, on peut se promener.
Si vous voulez, on peut échanger nos livres.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why did Marc write a note to Chloé?
choices: Because she was too loud after ten p.m.
Because she had taken his mail by mistake
Because he wanted to borrow a book
comprehension_questions.explanation: Marc wrote the note because Chloé's footsteps were very loud after ten p.m.

comprehension_questions.prompt: How does Chloé first react to the note?
choices: She feels offended, then understands Marc is right
She throws the note away without reading it
comprehension_questions.explanation: Chloé first feels offended, then sighs and admits Marc is right: she often dances late at night.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What does Chloé do after reading the note?
choices: She turns the music up louder
comprehension_questions.explanation: Chloé gathers her courage and goes upstairs to apologize directly to Marc.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What subject brings them together?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Chloé notices the books stacked near Marc's door and they discover their shared interest in reading.

comprehension_questions.prompt: How does the story end?
choices: They become friends and exchange books and messages
Marc moves away because of the noise
comprehension_questions.explanation: The noise hasn't completely disappeared, but they now exchange books and friendly texts instead of cold notes.

sentence_building.answer: Un matin, en sortant de chez elle, Chloé trouva un mot plié sous sa porte. « Vos pas sont très bruyants après vingt-deux heures. Merci de faire attention. »
sentence_building.translation: One morning, leaving her apartment, Chloé found a folded note under her door. "Your footsteps are very loud after ten p.m. Please be mindful."

sentence_building.answer: Marc lui rendit le prêt avec une bouteille de vin et une invitation: « Si vous voulez, on peut en discuter autour d'un verre. »
sentence_building.translation: Marc returned the loan with a bottle of wine and an invitation: "If you want, we can discuss it over a glass."

title: Un dimanche en Provence
summary: A solo traveler's plan to see lavender fields is disrupted by an unexpected invitation from a local innkeeper.

sentences.text: Thomas avait réservé une chambre d'hôtes au cœur de la Provence. Son plan était simple: louer un vélo et visiter les champs de lavande avant la foule estivale.
sentences.translation: Thomas had booked a guest room in the heart of Provence. His plan was simple: rent a bike and visit the lavender fields before the summer crowds.

sentences.text: À son arrivée, le village semblait endormi. Les champs de lavande s'étendaient à perte de vue, violets sous le ciel bleu.
sentences.translation: When he arrived, the village seemed asleep. The lavender fields stretched as far as the eye could see, purple under the blue sky.

sentences.text: L'aubergiste, une femme d'une soixantaine d'années, l'accueillit avec un sourire. Elle s'appelait Mireille et tenait la maison depuis trente ans.
sentences.translation: The innkeeper, a woman in her sixties, welcomed him with a smile. Her name was Mireille and she had run the house for thirty years.

sentences.text: « Je vous déconseille la route touristique aujourd'hui, » dit-elle en essuyant ses mains sur son tablier. « Il y a une fête de village à Saint-Rémy. »
sentences.translation: "I'd advise against the tourist road today," she said, drying her hands on her apron. "There's a village festival in Saint-Rémy."

sentences.text: Thomas hésita. Son guide indiquait un itinéraire précis, mais la chaleur devenait intense. « Que me conseillez-vous à la place ? » demanda-t-il.
sentences.translation: Thomas hesitated. His guidebook indicated a precise route, but the heat was becoming intense. "What do you recommend instead?" he asked.

sentences.text: « Restez ici. Je prépare un déjeuner sur la terrasse, et je vous raconte l'histoire du village. » Elle posa un plateau de fromages de chèvre et de tapenade sur la table.
sentences.translation: "Stay here. I'll prepare lunch on the terrace, and I'll tell you the story of the village." She placed a platter of goat cheeses and tapenade on the table.

sentences.text: Thomas accepta. Il s'installa sur la terrasse ombragée, un verre de rosé à la main, pendant que Mireille parlait des vendanges d'autrefois.
sentences.translation: Thomas accepted. He settled on the shaded terrace, a glass of rosé in hand, while Mireille talked about the grape harvests of the past.

sentences.text: Elle racontait les histoires de son grand-père, qui avait planté les premiers oliviers après la guerre. Thomas écoutait, fasciné.
sentences.translation: She told the stories of her grandfather, who had planted the first olive trees after the war. Thomas listened, fascinated.

sentences.text: « La lavande, vous la verrez demain, » dit-elle. « Mais un vrai repas provençal, avec quelqu'un qui connaît les recettes, ça ne se trouve pas dans les guides. »
sentences.translation: "You'll see the lavender tomorrow," she said. "But a real Provençal meal, with someone who knows the recipes — that you won't find in the guidebooks."

sentences.text: Après le déjeuner, Thomas l'aida à débarrasser. En lavant les assiettes, il réalisa que cette invitation impromptue valait mieux que n'importe quel itinéraire planifié.
sentences.translation: After lunch, Thomas helped her clear the table. While washing the dishes, he realized that this impromptu invitation was worth more than any planned itinerary.

sentences.text: Le lendemain, il pédala enfin vers les champs de lavande. Mais dans sa mémoire, le goût de la tapenade et les récits de Mireille resteraient plus longtemps que les photos.
sentences.translation: The next day, he finally cycled toward the lavender fields. But in his memory, the taste of the tapenade and Mireille's stories would stay longer than the photos.

example.text: L'aubergiste, une femme d'une soixantaine d'années, l'accueillit avec un sourire chaleureux.
example.translation: The innkeeper, a woman in her sixties, welcomed him with a warm smile.

example.text: Elle posa un plateau de fromages de chèvre et de tapenade sur la table.
example.translation: She placed a platter of goat cheeses and tapenade on the table.

example.text: Les champs de lavande s'étendaient à perte de vue, violets sous le ciel bleu.
example.translation: The lavender fields stretched as far as the eye could see, purple under the blue sky.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: L'aubergiste est très gentille et connaît bien la région.

language_notes.title: Giving advice with 'déconseiller'
language_notes.explanation: 'Déconseiller' is softer than 'ne fais pas' and is appropriate in service encounters between strangers.
language_notes.example: Je vous déconseille la route touristique aujourd'hui.
language_notes.example_translation: I'd advise against the tourist road today.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'déconseiller' to politely recommend against something.
variants: Je vous déconseille de sortir maintenant.
Je vous déconseille le plat du jour.

language_notes.title: Setting the scene with imparfait
language_notes.explanation: At B1, imparfait carries description and atmosphere. Passé composé or passé simple carry the narrative action.
language_notes.example: Le village semblait endormi. Les champs de lavande s'étendaient à perte de vue.
language_notes.example_translation: The village seemed asleep. The lavender fields stretched as far as the eye could see.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use imparfait for ongoing description, not completed action.
variants: La maison sentait bon la lavande.
Le soleil tapait fort sur les pierres.
Les cigales chantaient dans les arbres.

language_notes.title: Making a counter-suggestion with 'Que me conseillez-vous à la place?'
language_notes.explanation: This phrase transforms a rejection of advice into a constructive request, keeping the conversation open.
language_notes.example: Que me conseillez-vous à la place ?
language_notes.example_translation: What do you recommend instead?
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use this polite follow-up after someone advises against your plan.

language_notes.title: Expressing lasting value with 'rester dans la mémoire'
language_notes.explanation: This construction is useful for expressing emotional or sensory experiences that outlast practical ones.
language_notes.example: Le goût de la tapenade resterait plus longtemps que les photos.
language_notes.example_translation: The taste of the tapenade would stay longer than the photos.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'rester dans la mémoire' or 'rester plus longtemps que'
variants: Cette histoire restera dans ma mémoire.
Son sourire restera plus longtemps que ses paroles.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What was Thomas's initial plan?
choices: Rent a bike and see the lavender fields

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why does Mireille advise against the tourist road?

Because the road is closed for construction
Because there is no lavender this season

choices: To drive him there by car
Lunch on the terrace and the story of the village
comprehension_questions.explanation: Mireille offers to prepare lunch on the terrace and tell Thomas the story of the village.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What does Thomas learn during lunch?
choices: The stories of Mireille's grandfather who planted the first olive trees
The names of all the cheeses in the region
comprehension_questions.explanation: Mireille tells the stories of her grandfather, who had planted the first olive trees after the war.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What does Thomas remember most from that day?
choices: The perfect photos of the lavender fields
The taste of the tapenade and Mireille's stories
The difficulty of the tourist road
comprehension_questions.explanation: Thomas realizes that the taste of the tapenade and Mireille's stories will stay in his memory longer than the photos.

sentence_building.translation: When he arrived, the village seemed asleep. The lavender fields stretched as far as the eye could see, purple under the blue sky.

title: La carte postale
summary: A misdelivered postcard from 1985 leads a postal worker in a small Normandy town to unravel a love story the town forgot.

sentences.text: En triant le courrier du matin, Julie tomba sur une carte postale jaunie adressée à une adresse qui n'existait plus. Le village de Honfleur — rue des Pêcheurs, numéro quatorze.
sentences.translation: While sorting the morning mail, Julie came across a yellowed postcard addressed to an address that no longer existed. The village of Honfleur — Rue des Pêcheurs, number fourteen.

sentences.text: Julie était factrice depuis six ans dans ce village normand. Elle connaissait chaque rue, chaque boîte aux lettres, chaque nom de famille. Mais ce nom — Cardin — ne lui disait rien.
sentences.translation: Julie had been a postal worker for six years in this Norman village. She knew every street, every mailbox, every family name. But this name — Cardin — meant nothing to her.

sentences.text: Le timbre datait de 1985. L'encre, délavée mais lisible, portait un message bref : « Je pars demain. Je reviendrai. Je t'aime. » Il n'y avait pas de signature. Juste deux initiales : P.M.
sentences.translation: The stamp was dated 1985. The ink, faded but legible, bore a brief message: “I'm leaving tomorrow. I'll come back. I love you.” There was no signature. Just two initials: P.M.

sentences.text: Au lieu de jeter la carte au rebut, Julie la glissa dans la poche de sa veste. Quelque chose dans ce message — l'urgence, la vulnérabilité — la touchait plus qu'elle n'aurait su l'expliquer.
sentences.translation: Instead of throwing the card away, Julie slipped it into her jacket pocket. Something about this message — the urgency, the vulnerability — touched her more than she could explain.

sentences.text: Elle interrogea la boulangère, puis le patron du tabac. « Cardin ? Attendez... la vieille maison près du phare, avant la guerre. Mais personne n'y habite plus depuis des lustres. »
sentences.translation: She asked the baker, then the tobacco shop owner. "Cardin? Wait... the old house near the lighthouse, before the war. But no one has lived there for ages."

sentences.text: Julie ne se découragea pas. Elle voulait retrouver l'expéditeur ou le destinataire. Un après-midi, elle frappa à la porte de la Maison de retraite Saint-Joseph, la plus ancienne du village.
sentences.translation: Julie didn't get discouraged. She wanted to find the sender or the recipient. One afternoon, she knocked on the door of the Saint-Joseph retirement home, the oldest in the village.

sentences.text: Une vieille dame, Mathilde Cardin, reconnut l'écriture immédiatement. Ses doigts tremblèrent en touchant la carte. « C'est de Pierre, » murmura-t-elle. « Mon mari. Il m'a écrit juste avant de partir en mer. »
sentences.translation: An elderly lady, Mathilde Cardin, recognized the handwriting immediately. Her fingers trembled as she touched the card. "It's from Pierre," she murmured. "My husband. He wrote to me just before going out to sea."

sentences.text: Mathilde raconta son histoire : Pierre avait promis de revenir après une dernière saison de pêche. Il n'était jamais rentré. Le bateau avait disparu corps et biens en novembre 1985.
sentences.translation: Mathilde told her story: Pierre had promised to return after one last fishing season. He never came back. The ship had disappeared without a trace in November 1985.

sentences.text: « La carte n'est jamais arrivée, » dit Mathilde en essuyant ses yeux. « Pendant des années, j'ai cru qu'il était parti sans un mot. » Elle serra la carte contre sa poitrine. « Maintenant, je sais qu'il m'a écrit. »
sentences.translation: "The card never arrived," Mathilde said, wiping her eyes. "For years, I thought he had left without a word." She clutched the card to her chest. "Now I know he wrote to me."

sentences.text: Julie resta un moment silencieuse. Elle n'avait rien fait d'extraordinaire — juste son travail, avec un peu d'obstination. Mais ce simple geste avait apaisé une blessure vieille de plus de quarante ans.
sentences.translation: Julie stayed silent for a moment. She hadn't done anything extraordinary—just her job, with a bit of persistence. But this simple gesture had soothed a wound more than forty years old.

sentences.text: En sortant, Julie regarda le ciel gris de Honfleur. Le vent sentait le sel et l'iode. Le dernier message d'un marin de 1985 était enfin arrivé. Plus de quarante ans plus tard, mais il était arrivé.
sentences.translation: Leaving, Julie looked at the gray sky of Honfleur. The wind smelled of salt and iodine. A sailor's last message from 1985 had finally arrived—more than forty years late, but it had arrived.

example.text: En triant le courrier du matin, Julie tomba sur une carte postale jaunie adressée à une adresse qui n'existait plus.
example.translation: While sorting the morning mail, Julie came across a yellowed postcard addressed to an address that no longer existed.

example.text: Le timbre datait de 1985. L'encre, délavée mais lisible, portait un message bref: « Reviens. Je t'attends encore. »
example.translation: The stamp was dated 1985. The ink, faded but legible, bore a brief message: "Come back. I'm still waiting."

vocabulary.translation: to find again; to track down

language_notes.title: Expressing duration with 'depuis' + time expression
language_notes.explanation: At B2, 'depuis' with imperfect creates background context that explains a character's relationship to a place.
language_notes.example: Julie était factrice depuis six ans dans ce village normand.
language_notes.example_translation: Julie had been a postal worker for six years in this Norman village.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'depuis' + duration to describe how long something has been happening.
variants: Elle habite ici depuis trente ans.
Il travaille à la poste depuis 2018.

language_notes.title: Expressing rarity with 'depuis des lustres'
language_notes.explanation: 'Depuis des lustres' is a B2-level idiom that adds color to everyday French — far more expressive than 'depuis longtemps.'
language_notes.example: Personne n'y habite plus depuis des lustres.
language_notes.example_translation: No one has lived there for ages.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'depuis des lustres' as an idiomatic way to say 'for ages.'
variants: Je n'y suis pas allé depuis des lustres.
On ne s'est pas vus depuis des lustres.
La boutique est fermée depuis des lustres.

language_notes.title: Using 'corps et biens' as an idiom
language_notes.explanation: This fixed expression comes from maritime French and describes a disappearance where nothing — bodies or belongings — is ever recovered.
language_notes.example: Le bateau avait disparu corps et biens en novembre 1985.
language_notes.example_translation: The ship had disappeared without a trace in November 1985.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'disparaître corps et biens' for total disappearance.
variants: L'avion a disparu corps et biens.
L'équipage a disparu corps et biens.

language_notes.title: Describing emotional closure with 'refermer une blessure'
language_notes.explanation: This metaphor uses wound imagery for emotional closure — a sophisticated B2 narrative device.
language_notes.example: Ce simple geste avait refermé une blessure de quarante ans.
language_notes.example_translation: This simple gesture had healed a forty-year-old wound.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'refermer une blessure' metaphorically for emotional healing.
variants: Cette lettre a refermé une blessure ancienne.
Ses excuses ont refermé la blessure.

title: La fabrique du souvenir
summary: A granddaughter discovers that her grandmother's paintings in a Montmartre workshop hide a coded family history spanning two generations.

sentences.text: Dans l'atelier de sa grand-mère, au cœur de Montmartre, Emma découvrit un univers qu'elle n'avait jamais cherché à comprendre. Des toiles s'empilaient contre les murs, certaines achevées, d'autres à peine commencées.
sentences.translation: In her grandmother's studio, in the heart of Montmartre, Emma discovered a world she had never tried to understand. Canvases were stacked against the walls, some finished, others barely begun.

sentences.text: Sa grand-mère, Marguerite, était peintre depuis soixante ans. Ses œuvres ornaient quelques galeries du quartier, mais personne ne les avait jamais vraiment étudiées.
sentences.translation: Her grandmother, Marguerite, had been a painter for sixty years. Her works adorned a few galleries in the neighborhood, but no one had ever really studied them.

sentences.text: En rangeant l'atelier après le décès de Marguerite, Emma remarqua un détail étrange. Chaque toile portait des indices : un nom de rue gravé dans le cadre, une date minuscule sous un arbre, une initiale dans un coin de ciel.
sentences.translation: While tidying the studio after Marguerite's passing, Emma noticed a strange detail. Each canvas carried clues: a street name carved into the frame, a tiny date under a tree, an initial in a corner of sky.

sentences.text: Emma entreprit de les décrypter. Elle disposa les toiles par ordre chronologique des dates cachées. Un récit émergea : une histoire d'exil, un enfant laissé derrière, une promesse de retour jamais tenue.
sentences.translation: Emma set out to decipher them. She arranged the canvases in chronological order of the hidden dates. A narrative emerged: a story of exile, a child left behind, a promise of return never kept.

sentences.text: Elle comprit que sa grand-mère n'avait jamais cessé de peindre la même histoire : celle de son frère jumeau, perdu pendant la guerre, dont elle n'avait jamais retrouvé la trace.
sentences.translation: She understood that her grandmother had never stopped painting the same story: that of her twin brother, lost during the war, whose trace she had never found.

sentences.text: Pourquoi coder son histoire dans des tableaux au lieu de la raconter simplement ? Emma passa des heures à chercher une réponse. Puis elle trouva une lettre dans le tiroir du chevalet.
sentences.translation: Why encode her story in paintings instead of simply telling it? Emma spent hours searching for an answer. Then she found a letter in the easel drawer.

sentences.text: La lettre, écrite en 1944, expliquait tout : Marguerite avait promis à son frère de raconter leur histoire s'il ne revenait pas. Les tableaux étaient son témoignage.
sentences.translation: The letter, written in 1944, explained everything: Marguerite had promised her brother to tell their story if he never returned. The paintings were her testimony.

sentences.text: Emma se sentit traversée par le poids de ce silence de plus de quatre-vingts ans. Sa grand-mère n'avait jamais parlé de cette histoire. Elle l'avait peinte, jour après jour, toile après toile.
sentences.translation: Emma felt the weight of more than eighty years of silence. Her grandmother had never spoken of this story. She had painted it, day after day, canvas after canvas.

sentences.text: Elle décida de continuer le travail de sa grand-mère. Elle organisa une exposition : La Fabrique du souvenir. Les toiles de Marguerite y furent montrées dans l'ordre de leur code secret.
sentences.translation: She decided to continue her grandmother's work. She organized an exhibition: The Memory Factory. Marguerite's canvases were shown in the order of their secret code.

sentences.text: Les visiteurs voyaient des paysages de Montmartre. Mais Emma, elle, voyait enfin l'histoire que personne n'avait su lire. Parfois, le silence est la plus haute forme de mémoire.
sentences.translation: Visitors saw landscapes of Montmartre. But Emma, for her part, finally saw the story no one had known how to read. Sometimes, silence is the highest form of memory.

example.text: Dans l'atelier de sa grand-mere, au coeur de Montmartre, Emma decouvrit un univers qu'elle n'avait jamais cherche a comprendre.
example.translation: In her grandmother's studio, in the heart of Montmartre, Emma discovered a world she had never tried to understand.

example.text: Chaque toile portait des indices: un nom de rue grave dans le cadre, une date minuscule sous un arbre.
example.translation: Each canvas carried clues: a street name carved into the frame, a tiny date under a tree.

example.text: Elle avait transforme ses souvenirs en paysages, et chaque paysage contenait un message.
example.translation: She had transformed her memories into landscapes, and each landscape contained a message.

example.text: Pourquoi coder son histoire dans des tableaux au lieu de la raconter simplement?
example.translation: Why encode her story in paintings instead of simply telling it?

language_notes.title: Describing discovery with progressive detail
language_notes.explanation: This structure builds narrative suspense by revealing details progressively, a technique common in B2 literary description.
language_notes.example: En rangeant l'atelier apres le deces de Marguerite, Emma remarqua un detail etrange. Chaque toile portait des indices: un nom de rue, une date, une initiale.
language_notes.example_translation: While tidying the studio after Marguerite's passing, Emma noticed a strange detail. Each canvas carried clues: a street name, a date, an initial.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'En + gerund' followed by a colon-separated list for layered discovery.
variants: En lisant le journal, il trouva des informations: un lieu, un nom, une annee.
En ouvrant le tiroir, elle decouvrit des photos, des lettres, un carnet.

language_notes.title: Expressing purpose with 'au lieu de'
language_notes.explanation: 'Au lieu de' presents a choice between two actions, implying judgment about which would have been more straightforward.
language_notes.example: Pourquoi coder son histoire dans des tableaux au lieu de la raconter simplement?
language_notes.example_translation: Why encode her story in paintings instead of simply telling it?
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'au lieu de' to contrast what was done with what could have been done.
variants: Il a ecrit un livre au lieu de parler.
Elle a dessine au lieu d'expliquer.
Ils ont construit un mur au lieu de tendre la main.

language_notes.title: Expressing a turning point with 'Elle se sentit traversee par'
language_notes.explanation: This literary construction expresses an emotion that passes through the character, emphasizing its intensity and suddenness.
language_notes.example: Emma se sentit traversee par le poids de ce silence de soixante ans.
language_notes.example_translation: Emma felt pierced by the weight of this sixty-year silence.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'se sentir traverse par' for a sudden emotional or physical realization.
variants: Il se sentit traverse par une onde de choc.
Elle se sentit traversee par une certitude soudaine.
Je me suis senti traverse par la gravite du moment.

language_notes.title: Using apposition for compressed narrative
language_notes.explanation: The apposition 'elle' after the name creates a contrast between the subject and others, emphasizing her unique perspective.
language_notes.example: Les visiteurs voyaient des paysages de Montmartre. Mais Emma, elle, voyait enfin l'histoire que personne n'avait su lire.
language_notes.example_translation: Visitors saw landscapes of Montmartre. But Emma, for her part, finally saw the story no one had known how to read.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'elle' after the name for emphasis and contrast.
variants: Les autres parlaient. Lui, il observait.
Tout le monde croyait une version. Elle, elle savait.

title: Le débat en classe
summary: A heated classroom debate about secularism forces a quiet student in a French university seminar to take a public stand for the first time.

sentences.text: Le débat de la semaine portait sur la laïcité dans l'espace public, sujet particulièrement sensible dans cette université de la banlieue parisienne.
sentences.translation: The week's debate was about secularism in the public sphere, a sensitive topic at this university in the Paris suburbs.

sentences.text: Samia écoutait en silence, comme elle le faisait depuis le début du semestre. Elle prenait des notes, mais n'intervenait jamais. Le professeur, pourtant, l'observait.
sentences.translation: Samia listened in silence, as she had been doing since the start of the semester. She took notes but never spoke up. And yet, the professor watched her.

sentences.text: Antoine prit la parole le premier. « La laïcité, c'est la neutralité de l'État. Point. Les signes religieux n'ont pas leur place dans les services publics », affirma-t-il.
sentences.translation: Antoine spoke first. "Secularism means state neutrality. Period. Religious symbols have no place in public services," he asserted.

sentences.text: Plusieurs têtes opinèrent. Samia sentit son estomac se serrer. Elle leva la main, puis la baissa. Le professeur l'encouragea d'un signe.
sentences.translation: Several heads nodded. Samia felt her stomach tighten. She raised her hand, then lowered it. The professor encouraged her with a nod.

sentences.text: « Samia, vous semblez vouloir dire quelque chose, dit-il. La parole est libre dans ce séminaire. » Il y avait dans sa voix une invitation réelle, pas une pression rhétorique.
sentences.translation: "Samia, you seem to want to say something," he said. "Speech is free in this seminar." There was genuine invitation in his voice, not rhetorical pressure.

sentences.text: Pour la première fois de l'année, Samia prit la parole. Sa voix tremblait un peu, mais elle parla. « La laïcité, ce n'est pas l'absence de religion. C'est la garantie qu'aucune n'impose sa vérité aux autres. »
sentences.translation: For the first time all year, Samia spoke up. Her voice trembled a little, but she spoke. "Secularism isn't the absence of religion. It's the guarantee that none imposes its truth on others."

sentences.text: Antoine se tourna vers elle, surpris. « Donc vous êtes contre la neutralité des services publics ? » Samia soutint son regard. « Je suis pour une laïcité qui protège, pas qui exclut. C'est différent. »
sentences.translation: Antoine turned to her, surprised. "So you're against the neutrality of public services?" Samia held his gaze. "I'm for a secularism that protects, not one that excludes. That's different."

sentences.text: Le débat dura encore une heure. Samia intervint trois autres fois, gagnant en assurance à chaque prise de parole. Certains étudiants la regardaient autrement désormais.
sentences.translation: The debate lasted another hour. Samia intervened three more times, gaining confidence with each speech. Some students looked at her differently now.

sentences.text: En sortant, le professeur la rattrapa dans le couloir. « Vous avez bien fait de parler, Samia. Les idées s'affinent dans la confrontation, pas dans le silence. »
sentences.translation: As they left, the professor caught up with her in the hallway. "You did well to speak, Samia. Ideas are refined through confrontation, not silence."

sentences.text: Ce soir-là, Samia n'ouvrit pas ses livres. Elle repensait aux mots prononcés, aux regards posés sur elle. Elle avait pris position. Et elle n'avait pas tremblé, du moins pas jusqu'à ce que la porte de sa chambre se referme.
sentences.translation: That evening, Samia didn't open her books. She thought back to the words she had spoken, the looks toward her. She had taken a stand. And she hadn't trembled, at least not until her bedroom door closed.

example.text: Le débat de la semaine portait sur la laïcité dans l'espace public.
example.translation: The week's debate was about secularism in the public sphere.

example.text: Le débat de la semaine portait sur la laïcité dans l'espace public.
example.translation: The week's debate was about secularism in the public sphere.

language_notes.title: Defining a concept with ce n'est pas ... c'est ...
language_notes.explanation: This contrastive definition structure is a powerful rhetorical tool at B2. It establishes your position by first clearing away misconceptions.
language_notes.example: La laicite, ce n'est pas l'absence de religion. C'est la garantie qu'aucune n'impose sa verite.
language_notes.example_translation: Secularism isn't the absence of religion. It's the guarantee that none imposes its truth.
language_notes.pattern: [Concept], ce n'est pas [false definition]. C'est [true definition].
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use negative then positive definition for rhetorical effect.
variants: La liberte, ce n'est pas faire tout ce qu'on veut. C'est respecter celle des autres.
Le progres, ce n'est pas la technologie. C'est l'amelioration des conditions de vie.

language_notes.title: Expressing a shift from silence to speech
language_notes.explanation: This structure marks narrative turning points, the moment a character does something they never did before.
language_notes.example: Pour la premiere fois de l'annee, Samia prit la parole sans y avoir ete invitee par un exercice.
language_notes.example_translation: For the first time all year, Samia spoke up without being called on by an exercise.
language_notes.pattern: Pour la premiere fois de [time period], [subject] [verb]
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use pour la premiere fois to mark a turning point.
variants: Pour la premiere fois de sa vie, il a ose parler en public.
Pour la premiere fois du semestre, elle a leve la main.

language_notes.title: Expressing encouragement without pressure
language_notes.explanation: At B2, creating an environment of trust through declarative statements is as important as the arguments themselves.
language_notes.example: La parole est libre dans ce seminaire.
language_notes.example_translation: Speech is free in this seminar.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use a declarative statement about a space to invite participation.
variants: Ici, toutes les opinions sont bienvenues.
N'hesitez pas a prendre la parole.
Ce debat est un espace d'echange, pas de confrontation.

language_notes.title: Using s'affiner for intellectual refinement
language_notes.explanation: S'affiner describes a process of becoming sharper or more precise, ideal for intellectual and artistic contexts at B2.
language_notes.example: Les idees s'affinent dans la confrontation, pas dans le silence.
language_notes.example_translation: Ideas are refined through confrontation, not silence.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use s'affiner with dans for the context that refines.
variants: Le style s'affine dans la revision.

title: Le dîner de la discorde
summary: A wine choice at a family dinner in a bourgeois Parisian home escalates into a confrontation about an old betrayal.

sentences.text: Le dîner du dimanche chez les Montfort était une institution. Chaque semaine, la famille se réunissait autour d'une table d'acajou dans le seizième arrondissement.
sentences.translation: Sunday dinner at the Montforts' was an institution. Every week, the family gathered around a mahogany table in the sixteenth arrondissement.

sentences.text: Ce dimanche-là, Clara arriva la première, comme toujours. Sa mère disposait les couverts avec une précision chirurgicale. Son père lisait Le Figaro dans son fauteuil.
sentences.translation: That Sunday, Clara arrived first, as always. Her mother arranged the silverware with surgical precision. Her father read Le Figaro in his armchair.

sentences.text: Son frère, Antoine, entra avec une bouteille sous le bras. Il avait choisi un saint-émilion grand cru, un vin que leur père affectionnait particulièrement. Mais l'étiquette portait le nom d'un domaine que Clara connaissait bien.
sentences.translation: Her brother, Antoine, walked in with a bottle under his arm. He had chosen a Saint-Émilion grand cru, a wine their father particularly cherished. But the label bore the name of an estate Clara knew well.

sentences.text: Quand Antoine posa la bouteille sur la table, le silence se fit. Le père leva les yeux de son journal. La mère cessa de disposer les couverts. Clara sentit le sol se dérober sous elle.
sentences.translation: When Antoine placed the bottle on the table, silence fell. The father looked up from his newspaper. The mother stopped arranging the silverware. Clara felt the floor give way beneath her.

sentences.text: Le domaine en question appartenait à Hélène, l'ancienne associée de leur père. Elle avait quitté l'entreprise familiale dans des conditions que personne n'évoquait jamais ouvertement.
sentences.translation: The estate in question belonged to Hélène, their father's former business partner. She had left the family business under conditions that no one ever mentioned openly.

sentences.text: Pendant vingt ans, personne n'avait prononcé ce nom à table. Ce soir-là, un simple vin l'avait ramené à la surface. Clara fusilla son frère du regard.
sentences.translation: For twenty years, no one had uttered that name at the table. That evening, a simple wine had brought it back to the surface. Clara glared at her brother.

sentences.text: Antoine brisa le silence d'un ton faussement léger. « C'est un excellent millésime. Je me suis dit que cela ferait plaisir à tout le monde. »
sentences.translation: Antoine broke the silence with a falsely light tone. "It's an excellent vintage. I thought it would please everyone."

sentences.text: « Tu sais très bien ce que tu fais, » répondit Clara, la voix tremblante de colère contenue. « Cette bouteille n'est pas un hasard. »
sentences.translation: "You know very well what you're doing," Clara replied, her voice trembling with contained anger. "This bottle is not a coincidence."

sentences.text: Le père reposa son journal. Il regarda ses deux enfants, puis la bouteille. « Nous n'allons pas gâcher un dîner pour un vin, » dit-il. Mais la tension dans sa voix trahissait ses paroles.
sentences.translation: The father put down his newspaper. He looked at his two children, then at the bottle. "We're not going to ruin a dinner over a wine," he said. But the tension in his voice betrayed his words.

sentences.text: Le dîner se déroula dans une atmosphère électrique. Chaque bouchée semblait peser. La mère changea de sujet trois fois, sans succès. Le vin restait sur la table, ouvert mais intact dans les verres.
sentences.translation: Dinner unfolded in an electric atmosphere. Each bite seemed to weigh heavily. The mother changed the subject three times, without success. The wine sat on the table, opened but untouched in the glasses.

sentences.text: En partant, Clara attrapa Antoine par le bras dans l'entrée. « Pourquoi aujourd'hui ? Pourquoi ce vin ? » Il la regarda longuement. « Parce qu'il est temps que cette histoire sorte, Clara. Tu ne crois pas ? »
sentences.translation: As they left, Clara grabbed Antoine by the arm in the hallway. “Why today? Why this wine?” He looked at her for a long moment. “Because it's time this story came out, Clara. Don't you think?”

sentences.text: Clara ne répondit pas. Elle descendit l'escalier en pensant à toutes ces années de silence, aux dîners où l'on feignait d'ignorer ce que tout le monde savait. Peut-être qu'Antoine avait raison.
sentences.translation: Clara didn't answer. She walked down the stairs thinking about all those years of silence, the dinners where everyone pretended not to know what everyone knew. Maybe Antoine was right.

language_notes.title: Setting a scene of unspoken rules
language_notes.explanation: Calling something 'une institution' in French implies more than habit — it signals a ritual with social weight and unspoken expectations.
language_notes.example: Le dîner du dimanche chez les Montfort était une institution. Chaque semaine, la famille se réunissait autour d'une table d'acajou.
language_notes.example_translation: Sunday dinner at the Montforts' was an institution. Every week, the family gathered around a mahogany table.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'était une institution' to signal a ritual with unwritten rules.
variants: Le café du matin était une institution chez les Durand.
La promenade du soir était une institution dans ce village.
Le débat dominical était une institution dans leur famille.

language_notes.title: Expressing implicit accusation with 'tu sais très bien ce que tu fais'
language_notes.explanation: This construction accuses without naming the accusation — a sophisticated B2-level social maneuver that leaves the target to respond to the implication.
language_notes.example: Tu sais très bien ce que tu fais. Cette bouteille n'est pas un hasard.
language_notes.example_translation: You know very well what you're doing. This bottle is not a coincidence.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'tu sais très bien' to imply deliberate intent without direct accusation.
variants: Tu sais très bien pourquoi je suis là.
Tu sais très bien ce que cela signifie.
Tu sais très bien que ce n'est pas un accident.

language_notes.title: Describing studied ignorance with 'feindre d'ignorer'
language_notes.explanation: 'Feindre d'ignorer' captures a specific French social dynamic: the collective agreement to pretend not to know something everyone is aware of.
language_notes.example: Toutes ces années à feindre d'ignorer ce que tout le monde savait.
language_notes.example_translation: All those years pretending not to know what everyone knew.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'feindre d'ignorer' for deliberate, collective denial.
variants: Ils feignaient d'ignorer la gravité de la situation.

language_notes.title: Escalating tension with register shift
language_notes.explanation: At B2, register shifts between neutral description and charged observation create narrative tension without explicit drama.
language_notes.example: Le dîner se déroula dans une atmosphère électrique. Chaque bouchée semblait peser.
language_notes.example_translation: Dinner unfolded in an electric atmosphere. Each bite seemed to weigh heavily.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Shift from mundane description to emotional weight for tension.
variants: La conversation était anodine. Mais chaque mot semblait calculé.
Les plats étaient délicieux. Mais personne n'y touchait vraiment.

title: Le stage qui change tout
summary: A routine internship evaluation reveals a hidden tension between a mentor's advice and the CEO's expectations at a Paris startup.

sentences.text: À vingt-deux ans, Elias entamait son dernier mois de stage dans une start-up parisienne spécialisée dans l'analyse de données. L'ambiance y était jeune, mais la pression, elle, ne faisait que croître.
sentences.translation: At twenty-two, Elias was beginning his last month of internship at a Parisian startup specializing in data analysis. The atmosphere was young, but the pressure only grew.

sentences.text: L'évaluation de fin de stage devait être une simple formalité. Mais lorsque la directrice des ressources humaines l'invita dans son bureau, le ton de son courriel laissait présager autre chose.
sentences.translation: The end-of-internship evaluation was supposed to be a simple formality. But when the HR director invited him to her office, the tone of her email suggested otherwise.

sentences.text: Son parrain, Mehdi, lui avait toujours conseillé de ne pas trop en faire. « Reste discret, ne prends pas d'initiatives qui dépassent ta mission. » Elias avait suivi ce conseil à la lettre.
sentences.translation: His mentor, Mehdi, had always advised him not to overdo it. "Stay discreet, don't take initiatives that go beyond your assignment." Elias had followed this advice to the letter.

sentences.text: Dans le bureau, la DRH ne perdit pas de temps. « Elias, votre tuteur a rédigé un rapport très... mesuré. La direction s'interroge sur votre capacité à prendre des responsabilités. »
sentences.translation: In the office, the HR director did not waste time. "Elias, your supervisor has written a very... measured report. Management is questioning your ability to take on responsibilities."

sentences.text: Elias sentit un nœud se former dans son estomac. Il avait fait exactement ce que Mehdi lui avait dit. Et maintenant, on lui reprochait de ne pas en avoir fait assez.
sentences.translation: Elias felt a knot form in his stomach. He had done exactly what Mehdi had told him. And now, they were blaming him for not doing enough.

sentences.text: « Puis-je voir le rapport ? » demanda-t-il en s'efforçant de garder une voix calme. La DRH hésita, puis lui tendit une feuille imprimée.
sentences.translation: "May I see the report?" he asked, forcing himself to keep a calm voice. The HR director hesitated, then handed him a printed page.

sentences.text: « Elias a présenté des chiffres solides, mais son autonomie reste à prouver », lisait la première phrase. Plus bas: « Il exécute sans proposer. »
sentences.translation: "Elias has presented solid figures, but his autonomy remains to be proven," read the first sentence. Further down: "He executes without proposing."

sentences.text: En sortant du bureau, Elias croisa le PDG dans le couloir. « Elias, j'ai vu votre travail sur le tableau de bord client. Pourquoi ne l'avez-vous pas présenté en réunion ? »
sentences.translation: Leaving the office, Elias ran into the CEO in the hallway. "Elias, I saw your work on the client dashboard. Why didn't you present it in the meeting?"

sentences.text: Elias comprit alors le décalage: Mehdi lui avait appris la prudence, mais l'entreprise attendait de l'audace. Les deux stratégies s'opposaient sans que personne ne le lui ait dit clairement.
sentences.translation: Elias then understood the gap: Mehdi had taught him caution, but the company expected boldness. The two strategies opposed each other without anyone having told him clearly.

sentences.text: Il demanda un entretien avec Mehdi. La conversation fut difficile. « Je voulais te protéger, » expliqua ce dernier. « Mais tu as raison: j'aurais dû t'encourager à montrer ce dont tu es capable. »
sentences.translation: He asked for a meeting with Mehdi. The conversation was difficult. "I wanted to protect you," the latter explained. "But you're right: I should have encouraged you to show what you're capable of."

sentences.text: La semaine suivante, Elias prépara une présentation pour l'équipe dirigeante. Il y intégra ses propres analyses et proposa trois optimisations concrètes. L'accueil fut bien plus positif qu'il ne l'avait imaginé.
sentences.translation: The following week, Elias prepared a presentation for the management team. He included his own analyses and proposed three concrete optimizations. The reception was far more positive than he had imagined.

sentences.text: Le dernier jour, la DRH lui tendit une lettre de recommandation. « Nous serions ravis de vous revoir après vos études, Elias. Avec un peu plus d'initiative, vous irez loin. »
sentences.translation: On the last day, the HR director handed him a letter of recommendation. "We would be delighted to see you again after your studies, Elias. With a bit more initiative, you'll go far."

sentences.text: En rangeant son bureau, Elias repensa au conseil de Mehdi. Il comprit que la loyauté et l'ambition ne s'opposent pas toujours — à condition de savoir quand appliquer l'une ou l'autre.
sentences.translation: While clearing his desk, Elias thought back to Mehdi's advice. He understood that loyalty and ambition don't always oppose each other — provided you know when to apply one or the other.

example.text: À vingt-deux ans, Elias entamait son dernier mois de stage dans une start-up parisienne spécialisée dans l'analyse de données.
example.translation: At twenty-two, Elias was beginning his last month of internship at a Parisian startup specializing in data analysis.

example.text: L'évaluation de mi-parcours devait être une simple formalité.
example.translation: The mid-term evaluation was supposed to be a simple formality.

example.text: Son parrain, Mehdi, lui avait toujours conseillé de ne pas trop en faire.
example.translation: His mentor, Mehdi, had always advised him not to overdo it.

example.text: « Elias a présenté des chiffres solides, mais son autonomie reste à prouver », lisait la première phrase du rapport.
example.translation: "Elias has presented solid figures, but his autonomy remains to be proven," read the first sentence of the report.

example.text: « Elias a présenté des chiffres solides, mais son autonomie reste à prouver », lisait la première phrase du rapport.
example.translation: "Elias has presented solid figures, but his autonomy remains to be proven," read the first sentence of the report.

language_notes.title: Expressing implicit criticism in professional French
language_notes.explanation: In B2 professional French, criticism is often embedded in a 'mais' clause after an initial positive statement — a technique called 'la critique en sandwich.'
language_notes.example: Elias a présenté des chiffres solides, mais son autonomie reste à prouver.
language_notes.example_translation: Elias has presented solid figures, but his autonomy remains to be proven.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'mais' after a compliment to introduce a hidden criticism.
variants: Votre travail est bon, mais votre ponctualité laisse à désirer.
Le rapport est complet, mais la synthèse manque de clarté.
Vous êtes compétent, mais votre communication pourrait être améliorée.

language_notes.title: Reporting indirect speech in workplace context
language_notes.explanation: At B2, indirect speech allows characters to convey criticism without direct confrontation — reflecting real workplace communication.
language_notes.example: La DRH lui dit que la direction s'interroge sur sa capacité à prendre des responsabilités.
language_notes.example_translation: The HR director told him that management is questioning his ability to take on responsibilities.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'que' to report what someone said without direct quotation.
variants: Il a dit que le projet était en retard.
Elle a expliqué que les objectifs avaient changé.
Le rapport indique que les résultats sont encourageants.

language_notes.title: Expressing obligation with 'rester à' + infinitive
language_notes.explanation: This construction is common in French professional evaluations — it marks something as pending without being accusatory.
language_notes.example: Son autonomie reste à prouver.
language_notes.example_translation: His autonomy remains to be proven.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'rester à' + infinitive to indicate something still needs to be done.

language_notes.title: Contrasting two approaches with 'tandis que' and 'alors que'
language_notes.explanation: These connectors are essential at B2 for articulating nuanced professional contrasts.
language_notes.example: Mehdi lui avait appris la prudence, alors que l'entreprise attendait de l'audace.
language_notes.example_translation: Mehdi had taught him caution, while the company expected boldness.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'alors que' or 'tandis que' to highlight opposing approaches.
variants: Il préférait la discrétion, tandis que ses collègues cherchaient la visibilité.
Elle pensait sécurité d'abord, alors que la direction voulait de l'innovation.

title: Les coulisses du journal
summary: A junior reporter at a regional newspaper must decide whether to publish a story that implicates her editor's close friend.

sentences.text: Au journal régional Le Dauphiné, Inès préparait son premier sujet d'investigation sérieux. Depuis trois semaines, elle recoupait des documents sur un marché public attribué dans des conditions douteuses.
sentences.translation: At the regional newspaper Le Dauphiné, Inès was preparing her first serious investigation piece. For three weeks, she had been cross-referencing documents about a public contract awarded under questionable circumstances.

sentences.text: Son rédacteur en chef, Paul, l'avait prise sous son aile dès son arrivée. Il était exigeant mais juste, et Inès respectait son jugement plus que tout.
sentences.translation: Her editor-in-chief, Paul, had taken her under his wing from day one. He was demanding but fair, and Inès respected his judgment above all else.

sentences.text: « Inès, ton enquête sur les marchés publics est solide, » dit-il en feuilletant les pages. « Mais il y a un problème. » Il marqua une pause. « Le principal mis en cause est un ami personnel. »
sentences.translation: "Inès, your investigation on public contracts is solid," he said, flipping through the pages. "But there's a problem." He paused. "The main person implicated is a personal friend."

sentences.text: Inès resta silencieuse. Elle comprit immédiatement la portée de ce qu'il venait de dire. Paul ne lui demandait pas explicitement d'enterrer l'article. Mais le sous-entendu était clair.
sentences.translation: Inès remained silent. She immediately understood the weight of what he had just said. Paul wasn't explicitly asking her to bury the article. But the implication was clear.

sentences.text: « J'ai vérifié toutes mes sources, » insista-t-elle. « Les documents sont authentiques. Si on ne publie pas, c'est la déontologie qu'on trahit. »
sentences.translation: "I've checked all my sources," she insisted. "The documents are authentic. If we don't publish, we're betraying journalistic ethics."

sentences.text: Paul se frotta les tempes. « On ne peut pas publier ça. Pas comme ça. Pas maintenant. » Il n'ajouta rien. Le silence entre eux devint lourd, chargé de tout ce qui ne pouvait pas être dit.
sentences.translation: Paul rubbed his temples. "We can't publish this. Not like this. Not now." He added nothing. The silence between them became heavy, charged with everything that couldn't be said.

sentences.text: Cette nuit-là, Inès ne dormit pas. Elle repensait aux visages des personnes citées dans l'enquête, au droit du public à savoir, à la carrière de Paul, à la sienne.
sentences.translation: That night, Inès didn't sleep. She kept thinking about the faces of the people cited in the investigation, the public's right to know, Paul's career, her own.

sentences.text: Le lendemain, elle prit une décision. Elle proposa de confier l'article à une rédactrice indépendante et de signaler officiellement le conflit d'intérêts de Paul.
sentences.translation: The next day, she made a decision. She proposed entrusting the article to an independent editor and formally disclosing Paul's conflict of interest.

sentences.text: Paul lut la proposition sans rien dire. Puis il hocha lentement la tête. « C'est la bonne procédure. Je vais me retirer du dossier et prévenir la direction. »
sentences.translation: Paul read the proposal without saying anything. Then he slowly nodded. “That's the right procedure. I'll step away from the story and inform management.”

sentences.text: Après une nouvelle vérification, l'article parut en une le jeudi suivant avec les faits et les noms nécessaires. Le journal reçut un appel du cabinet du maire dès le matin.
sentences.translation: After another round of verification, the article appeared on the front page the following Thursday with the necessary facts and names. The paper received a call from the mayor's office that morning.

sentences.text: Paul ne félicita jamais Inès ouvertement. Mais en quittant le bureau ce soir-là, il laissa sur son clavier un mot : « Tu as fait le bon choix. Le métier, parfois, c'est savoir se retirer pour protéger une enquête. »
sentences.translation: Paul never openly congratulated Inès. But as he left the office that evening, he left a note on her keyboard: “You made the right choice. Sometimes this job means knowing when to step aside to protect an investigation.”

example.text: Au journal régional Le Dauphiné, Inès préparait son premier sujet d'investigation sérieux.
example.translation: At the regional newspaper Le Dauphiné, Inès was preparing her first serious investigation piece.

example.text: « Inès, ton enquête sur les marchés publics est solide, » dit-il en feuilletant les pages. « Mais il y a un problème. »
example.translation: "Inès, your investigation on public contracts is solid," he said, flipping through the pages. "But there's a problem."

example.text: « J'ai vérifié toutes mes sources, » insista-t-elle. « Les documents sont authentiques. »
example.translation: "I've checked all my sources," she insisted. "The documents are authentic."

example.text: « On ne peut pas publier ça. Pas comme ça. Pas maintenant. »
example.translation: "We can't publish this. Not like this. Not now."

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: L'enquête a révélé des irrégularités dans les marchés publics.
Un journaliste doit protéger ses sources.
La déontologie journalistique exige de vérifier ses sources.

language_notes.title: Reporting without naming — ethical compromise vocabulary
language_notes.explanation: This construction is common in B2-level journalism and legal French — it reports facts without explicit accusation.
language_notes.example: L'article ne mentionnait aucun nom directement, mais les faits parlaient d'eux-mêmes.
language_notes.example_translation: The article didn't mention any names directly, but the facts spoke for themselves.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'ne...aucun' + 'mais' for ethical reporting language.
variants: Le rapport ne cite aucun nom, mais les preuves sont claires.
Elle n'accuse personne directement, mais les faits sont accablants.
L'article ne révèle pas la source, mais les informations sont vérifiées.

language_notes.title: Expressing an unspoken implication with 'le sous-entendu'
language_notes.explanation: 'Sous-entendu' is a key word at B2 — it names the gap between what is said and what is meant, a cornerstone of implicit French communication.
language_notes.example: Paul ne lui demandait pas explicitement d'enterrer l'article. Mais le sous-entendu était clair.
language_notes.example_translation: Paul wasn't explicitly asking her to bury the article. But the implication was clear.
language_notes.pattern: [statement of what wasn't said] + mais le sous-entendu [was clear]
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'le sous-entendu' to name what is implied but not stated.
variants: Il n'a pas refusé directement. Mais le sous-entendu était là.
Elle n'a pas dit non. Mais le sous-entendu pesait.

language_notes.title: Making an ethical argument with 'c'est... qu'on trahit'
language_notes.explanation: The 'c'est... que' structure emphasizes the object of the verb, giving rhetorical weight to ethical arguments.
language_notes.example: Si on ne publie pas, c'est la déontologie qu'on trahit.
language_notes.example_translation: If we don't publish, it's journalistic ethics we betray.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'c'est... que' to emphasize the ethical principle at stake.
variants: C'est la confiance du public qu'on perd.
C'est la vérité qu'on doit défendre.

language_notes.title: Expressing a limit with 'savoir jusqu'où ne pas aller'
language_notes.explanation: This idiomatic construction expresses professional wisdom about boundaries — a subtle and sophisticated B2-level expression.
language_notes.example: Le métier, parfois, c'est savoir jusqu'où ne pas aller.
language_notes.example_translation: The job, sometimes, is knowing how far not to go.
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'savoir jusqu'où ne pas' for knowing one's boundaries.

title: Al Mercato
summary: Giulia strolls through the vibrant stalls of Campo de' Fiori, where the air is filled with the scent of fresh produce and flowers.

sentences.text: È sabato mattina e Giulia va al mercato di Campo de' Fiori, a Roma.
sentences.translation: It's Saturday morning and Giulia heads to the bustling Campo de' Fiori market in Rome.

sentences.text: Il mercato è all'aperto e ci sono molti banchi colorati.
sentences.translation: The market is outdoors, alive with vibrant, colorful stalls.

sentences.text: Giulia vede frutta fresca, verdura, fiori e formaggi. " Buongiorno, signora! Cosa desidera?" chiede il venditore. "
sentences.translation: Giulia sees fresh fruit, vegetables, flowers, and cheeses. " Good morning, ma'am! What would you like?" asks the cheerful seller. "

sentences.text: Vorrei un chilo di pomodori e mezzo chilo di peperoni rossi, per favore," dice Giulia.
sentences.translation: I'd like a kilo of tomatoes and half a kilo of red peppers, please," Giulia replies.

sentences.text: I pomodori sono rossi e profumati. Giulia compra anche delle fragole dolci e un mazzo di basilico fresco.
sentences.translation: The tomatoes are red and fragrant, bursting with aroma. Giulia also picks up sweet strawberries and a bunch of fresh basil.

sentences.text: "Il basilico è in regalo oggi," dice il venditore con un sorriso. Giulia paga e mette tutto nella sua borsa di stoffa.
sentences.translation: "The basil is a gift today," the seller says with a warm smile. Giulia pays and tucks everything into her cloth bag.

sentences.text: Cammina tra i banchi e compra anche del pane fresco e della mozzarella.
sentences.translation: She strolls between stalls, also buying fresh bread and mozzarella.

sentences.text: Quando torna a casa, Giulia prepara un'insalata caprese con i pomodori, la mozzarella e il basilico. È semplice ma deliziosa.
sentences.translation: Back home, Giulia prepares a caprese salad with tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil. It's simple yet delicious.

title: La Colazione da Marta
summary: A regular customer's usual order is accidentally swapped, leading to a pleasant breakfast discovery in Naples.

sentences.text: Tutti i giorni Marco va al bar "Da Marta" per la colazione, prima di andare in ufficio.
sentences.translation: Every day Marco goes to the bar "Da Marta" for breakfast, before going to the office.

sentences.text: Marta lavora come barista da vent'anni e conosce tutti i clienti.
sentences.translation: Marta has worked as a barista for twenty years and knows all the customers.

sentences.text: Marco è un cliente fedele. Ordina sempre la stessa cosa.
sentences.translation: Marco is a loyal customer. He always orders the same thing.

sentences.text: Per lui è un cappuccino e una brioche alla crema. Ogni giorno, da anni.
sentences.translation: For him it's a cappuccino and a cream-filled croissant. Every day, for years.

sentences.text: Ma oggi qualcosa cambia. Marco dice: "Buongiorno, Marta! Il solito, per favore."
sentences.translation: But today something changes. Marco says: "Good morning, Marta! The usual, please."

sentences.text: Marta è molto occupata e per sbaglio prende una brioche con la marmellata, non alla crema.
sentences.translation: Marta is very busy and by mistake she takes a croissant with jam, not cream-filled.

sentences.text: Marco prende il cappuccino, la brioche e va al suo tavolo vicino alla finestra.
sentences.translation: Marco takes the cappuccino, the croissant and goes to his table near the window.

sentences.text: Morde la brioche e fa una faccia strana. "Questa non è alla crema, è alla marmellata!"
sentences.translation: He bites the croissant and makes a strange face. "This isn't cream-filled, it's with jam!"

sentences.text: Ma poi sorride. La marmellata di albicocche è calda e dolce. "Che buona!" pensa.
sentences.translation: But then he smiles. The apricot jam is warm and sweet. "How good!" he thinks.

sentences.text: Marta si avvicina e dice: "Scusa, Marco! Ho sbagliato. Vuoi un'altra brioche?"
sentences.translation: Marta approaches and says: "Sorry, Marco! I made a mistake. Do you want another croissant?"

sentences.text: Marco ride. "No, va bene così. Scoprire un gusto nuovo è bello. La marmellata di albicocche è deliziosa!"
sentences.translation: Marco laughs. "No, it's fine like this. Discovering a new taste is nice. The apricot jam is delicious!"

example.translation: For him it's a cappuccino and a cream-filled croissant

language_notes.title: Ordering the usual
language_notes.explanation: 'Il solito' is a very common Italian expression for regulars at bars and restaurants.
language_notes.example: Il solito, per favore
language_notes.example_translation: The usual, please
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'il solito' when you always order the same thing.

language_notes.title: Apologizing for a mistake
language_notes.explanation: 'Ho sbagliato' means 'I was wrong / I made a mistake'. Use 'Scusa' informally with friends.
language_notes.example: Scusa, Marco! Ho sbagliato
language_notes.example_translation: Sorry, Marco! I made a mistake
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'Ho sbagliato' to admit you made an error.

language_notes.title: Saying it's fine / no problem
language_notes.explanation: 'Va bene così' is a useful phrase when you want to say something is acceptable as it is.
language_notes.example: Va bene così
language_notes.example_translation: It's fine like this
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'va bene così' to accept something as it is.

language_notes.title: Expressing that something is good to eat
language_notes.explanation: 'Che buono/buona!' is a common exclamation for food. Match the gender of the food.
language_notes.example: Che buona!
language_notes.example_translation: How good (it is)!
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'Che' + adjective to express how good something is.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What happens differently today?

comprehension_questions.prompt: How does Marco react when he discovers the mistake?
choices: He smiles and says it's good
comprehension_questions.explanation: Marco smiles and thinks: "The apricot jam is warm and sweet. How good!"

comprehension_questions.prompt: What flavor of jam is in the brioche?
comprehension_questions.explanation: The jam is apricot, warm and sweet.

title: La Gita al Mercato
summary: A child's shopping list turns a routine errand into a negotiation with every vendor at the Roman market.

sentences.text: È sabato mattina e Sofia va al mercato con la sua mamma e il fratello Luca.
sentences.translation: It's Saturday morning and Sofia goes to the market with her mom and her brother Luca.

sentences.text: Sofia ha una lista della spesa lunga un metro, piena di disegni colorati.
sentences.translation: Sofia has a shopping list a meter long, full of colorful drawings.

sentences.text: Davanti alla pescheria c'è una signora che grida: "Pesce fresco, oggi!"
sentences.translation: In front of the fish shop there is a woman who shouts: "Fresh fish today!"

sentences.text: Luca tira la mamma per la maglia. "Mamma, io voglio vedere i pesci!"
sentences.translation: Luca pulls mom by the shirt. "Mom, I want to see the fish!"

sentences.text: Sofia controlla la lista e dice: "Prima le carote e le zucchine, poi i pesci."
sentences.translation: Sofia checks the list and says: "First the carrots and zucchinis, then the fish."

sentences.text: Al banco della frutta, Luca sorride e chiede: "Quanto costa un chilo di mele?"
sentences.translation: At the fruit stall, Luca smiles and asks: "How much is a kilo of apples?"

sentences.text: Il venditore risponde: "Due euro, piccolo. Per te, un euro e cinquanta!"
sentences.translation: The seller answers: "Two euros, little one. For you, one euro and fifty!"

sentences.text: Sofia guarda la mamma. "Mamma, le fragole costano poco. Possiamo comprarle?"
sentences.translation: Sofia looks at mom. "Mom, strawberries cost little. Can we buy them?"

sentences.text: La mamma ride e dice di sì. Luca sceglie anche un'anguria enorme per dopo pranzo.
sentences.translation: Mom laughs and says yes. Luca also picks an enormous watermelon for after lunch.

sentences.text: Tornano a casa con le borse piene. "Che bella gita al mercato!" dice Sofia. "E domani si ricomincia!"
sentences.translation: They return home with full bags. "What a nice trip to the market!" says Sofia. "And tomorrow we start again!"

language_notes.title: Asking about prices
language_notes.explanation: 'Quanto costa' is the most common way to ask about the price of something. Use 'Quanto costano' for plural items.
language_notes.example: Quanto costa un chilo di mele?
language_notes.example_translation: How much is a kilo of apples?
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'Quanto costa' + item to ask about price.
variants: Quanto costa un chilo di pomodori?
Quanto costa un mazzo di fiori?

language_notes.title: Saying what you want to do
language_notes.explanation: 'Voglio' (I want) is a useful modal verb. It's always followed by an infinitive.
language_notes.example: Io voglio vedere i pesci
language_notes.example_translation: I want to see the fish
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'voglio' + infinitive to express what you want.

language_notes.title: Talking about quantities
language_notes.explanation: When buying food, use 'di' between the quantity and the item.
language_notes.example: Un chilo di mele
language_notes.example_translation: A kilo of apples
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use '[quantity] di [item]' to specify amounts.

language_notes.title: Expressing agreement
language_notes.explanation: 'Dire di sì' is the standard way to express agreement or say yes to a request in Italian.
language_notes.example: La mamma ride e dice di sì
language_notes.example_translation: Mom laughs and says yes
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'dire di sì' to say yes to a request.

title: La pizzeria di quartiere
summary: Matteo scivola nella pizzeria di quartiere, dove il profumo di basilico e crosta dorata lo avvolge, mentre Claudia gli sorride da dietro il bancone.

sentences.text: Venerdì sera Matteo entra nella piccola pizzeria alla fine della strada, stanco dopo il lungo turno al negozio.
sentences.translation: On Friday evening, Matteo steps into the small pizzeria at the end of the street, weary after a long shift at the store.

sentences.text: Il forno a legna emana un profumo dolce di pomodoro e mozzarella calda sulla pasta sottile.
sentences.translation: The wood-fired oven releases a sweet aroma of tomato and warm mozzarella on thin dough.

sentences.text: Claudia sorride da dietro il bancone e chiede: "Margherita come sempre?"
sentences.translation: Claudia smiles from behind the counter and asks, "Margherita as usual?"

sentences.text: Matteo annuisce, ma chiede più basilico fresco perché ha imparato la parola ieri.
sentences.translation: Matteo nods, but asks for more fresh basil because he learned the word yesterday.

sentences.text: Claudia annuisce, stende l'impasto sottile, passa la paletta sotto la pizza e la taglia in quattro spicchi caldi.
sentences.translation: Claudia nods, stretches the thin dough, slides the peel under the pizza, and cuts it into four hot slices.

sentences.text: Matteo paga alla cassa, prende la scatola di cartone e annusa il profumo caldo mentre cammina verso casa.
sentences.translation: Matteo pays at the register, takes the cardboard box, and inhales the warm aroma as he walks home.

title: Una domenica al parco
summary: Giulia spreads a blanket beside the duck pond, trades quiet chat with Luca, and notes three verbs that bookmark the smallest kind of fluent Sunday.

sentences.text: Domenica mattina, Giulia cammina lentamente verso il parco vicino a casa sua con una borsa di tela e un libro sottile.
sentences.translation: On Sunday morning, Giulia strolls slowly toward the park near her home, carrying a canvas tote and a slim book.

sentences.text: Il sole filtra delicato tra le foglie degli alberi, mentre alcuni bambini inseguono una palla rossa che rimbalza sull'erba.
sentences.translation: The sun gently filters through the leaves of the trees, while children chase a red ball bouncing on the grass.

sentences.text: Lei sceglie una panchina libera accanto allo stagno, dove le anatre nuotano in silenzio, e un signore anziano lancia briciole di pane
sentences.translation: She chooses a free bench next to the pond, where ducks swim silently, and an elderly man tosses breadcrumbs to

sentences.text: Lei risponde di sì, ma confessa che oggi preferisce osservare le foglie che leggere ogni pagina.
sentences.translation: She says yes, but admits that today she prefers watching the leaves to reading every page.

sentences.text: Prima di tornare a casa, scrive sulla copertina del libro tre parole italiane che le piacciono, così lunedì al lavoro ricorderà meglio

title: Una Passeggiata a Roma
summary: A tourist trying to find the Trevi Fountain learns more from getting lost than from the map.

sentences.text: Anna è in vacanza a Roma. È il suo primo giorno e vuole vedere la Fontana di Trevi.
sentences.translation: Anna is on vacation in Rome. It's her first day and she wants to see the Trevi Fountain.

sentences.text: Prende la mappa dall'hotel e cammina per le strade del centro.
sentences.translation: She takes the map from the hotel and walks through the streets of the center.

sentences.text: Le strade sono strette e piene di persone. Anna guarda la mappa, ma non capisce bene.
sentences.translation: The streets are narrow and full of people. Anna looks at the map, but she doesn't understand well.

sentences.text: Una guida locale sorride e chiede: "Hai bisogno di aiuto?"
sentences.translation: A local guide smiles and asks: "Do you need help?"

sentences.text: Anna risponde: "Sì, grazie. Cerco la Fontana di Trevi, ma mi sono persa."
sentences.translation: Anna answers: "Yes, thanks. I'm looking for the Trevi Fountain, but I got lost."

sentences.text: La guida dice: "Non è lontana. Prima, però, guarda questa piazza bellissima con una fontana antica."
sentences.translation: The guide says: "It's not far. First, though, look at this beautiful square with an ancient fountain."

sentences.text: Anna guarda la piazza. È piena di fiori, persone e musica da lontano.
sentences.translation: Anna looks at the square. It's full of flowers, people and music from afar.

sentences.text: La guida continua: "Adesso gira a destra, poi sempre dritto. Dopo due minuti, vedi la fontana."
sentences.translation: The guide continues: "Now turn right, then straight ahead. After two minutes, you'll see the fountain."

sentences.text: Anna segue le indicazioni e arriva alla Fontana di Trevi. È enorme e bellissima.
sentences.translation: Anna follows the directions and arrives at the Trevi Fountain. It's enormous and beautiful.

sentences.text: Guarda l'acqua blu e le statue bianche. "Che meraviglia!" dice.
sentences.translation: She looks at the blue water and the white statues. "How wonderful!" she says.

sentences.text: Anna lancia una moneta nell'acqua, come fanno tutti i turisti.
sentences.translation: Anna throws a coin into the water, as all tourists do.

sentences.text: Poi pensa: "Mi sono persa, ma ho visto cose bellissime. Qualche volta perdersi è bello!"
sentences.translation: Then she thinks: "I got lost, but I saw beautiful things. Sometimes getting lost is nice!"

language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'avere bisogno di' to express needing something.
