L'ospitalità siciliana è leggendaria.

language_notes.title: Trapassato prossimo for backstory
language_notes.explanation: The trapassato prossimo sets the background context in past narratives — what had already happened before the main story begins.
language_notes.example: era stato organizzato con tre mesi di anticipo
language_notes.example_translation: had been organized three months in advance
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use trapassato prossimo (era stato + past participle) for actions completed before another past event.

language_notes.title: Expressing cancellation and change of plans
language_notes.explanation: The passive voice with 'essere' is common in Italian for describing service disruptions.
language_notes.example: Il volo di ritorno è stato cancellato
language_notes.example_translation: The return flight was canceled
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use passive 'è stato cancellato' to describe an event beyond anyone's control.

language_notes.title: The hypothetical 'come se' + congiuntivo imperfetto
language_notes.explanation: 'Come se' requires the subjunctive imperfect, even when referring to present situations.
language_notes.example: come se si conoscessero da sempre
language_notes.example_translation: as if they had known each other forever
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'come se' + congiuntivo imperfetto for unreal or hypothetical comparisons.
variants: Si comporta come fosse a casa sua

language_notes.title: Idiomatic: Alla prossima
language_notes.explanation: 'Alla prossima' is short for 'alla prossima volta' and conveys warmth and anticipation of meeting again.
language_notes.example: Alla prossima
language_notes.example_translation: Until next time
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use 'Alla prossima' as a friendly, informal goodbye that implies future meetings.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why was the house exchange planned three months in advance?
choices: Because the two families had never spoken before
To ensure precise departure and arrival dates for both
Because the houses were in two different and distant cities
comprehension_questions.explanation: The exchange was organized three months in advance with precise dates: the Romanos leave on August 1st, the Rizzutos on the 15th.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What do the Romanos find when they arrive in Palermo?
choices: An empty house with keys under the mat
The Rizzuto family still in the house with the light on and music from the balcony
An apology note and a bouquet of flowers
comprehension_questions.explanation: The Romanos find the light on and Sicilian music from the balcony — the Rizzutos are still there because their return flight was canceled.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What compromise do the two families reach?
choices: The Romanos sleep in a hotel paid by the Rizzutos
They organize a dinner together and share the house for two days
The Rizzutos leave immediately by car
comprehension_questions.explanation: They find a compromise: sharing the house for two days and preparing a dinner together — pasta alla Norma for the Romanos, carbonara for the Rizzutos.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What do the Rizzutos leave when they finally leave?
choices: A note saying "The couch is always free"
comprehension_questions.explanation: The Rizzutos leave a note: "The house is yours. But if you come back to Palermo, the couch is always free."

comprehension_questions.prompt: What do the Romanos find upon their return to Rome?
choices: A package of Sicilian cookies with a thank-you note
comprehension_questions.explanation: They find a package of Sicilian cookies on the table with a note: "Thanks for dinner. See you next time."

comprehension_questions.prompt: Sfida: Perché lo scambio di case, nonostante l'inconveniente, si trasforma in un'esperienza positiva?
choices: Perché i Rizzuto pagano il conto del ristorante
Perché entrambe le famiglie scelgono la flessibilità e l'ospitalità invece del conflitto
Perché il volo cancellato era una coincidence fortunata
comprehension_questions.explanation: Invece di litigare, le famiglie trasformano un imprevisto in un'occasione di convivialità, dimostrando che la vera ospitalità italiana supera ogni inconveniente.

sentence_building.answer: I Romano dovevano arrivare a Palermo il primo agosto, proprio quando i Rizzuto sarebbero partiti per Roma. Tutto sembrava perfetto.
sentence_building.translation: The Romanos were due to arrive in Palermo on August first, just as the Rizzutos were supposed to leave for Rome. Everything seemed perfect.

sentence_building.answer: Il giorno dopo, i Rizzuto partono davvero. Ma prima, lasciano un biglietto: "La casa è vostra. Ma se tornate a Palermo, il divano è sempre libero."
sentence_building.translation: The next day, the Rizzutos really leave. But first, they leave a note: "The house is yours. But if you come back to Palermo, the sofa is always free."

title: 마지막 창가 자리
subtitle: The Last Window Seat
summary: At a noisy Hongdae café, Junho must change his order quickly if he wants the last seat by the rain-streaked window.
setting_tags: A café near Hongik University Station
communicative_outcome: Order a drink, change one detail, and ask whether a seat is free.

sentences.text: 비 오는 오후, 준호는 홍대 앞 작은 카페에 들어가요.
sentences.translation: On a rainy afternoon, Junho steps into a small café in Hongdae.

sentences.text: 커피 기계 소리 사이로 창가 자리 하나가 보여요.
sentences.translation: Through the noise of the coffee grinder, he spots one window seat.

sentences.text: 준호는 “따뜻한 라테 한 잔 주세요”라고 주문해요.
sentences.translation: Junho orders, “One hot latte, please.”

sentences.text: 직원은 “죄송하지만 우유가 없어요”라고 말해요.
sentences.translation: The barista says, “I’m sorry, but we’re out of milk.”

sentences.text: 준호는 잠깐 생각하고 “그럼 우유 대신 두유로 주세요”라고 해요.
sentences.translation: Junho thinks for a moment, then says, “Then soy milk instead, please.”

sentences.text: 창가에 앉은 손님에게 “여기 자리 있어요?”라고 물어요.
sentences.translation: He asks the customer by the window, “Is this seat taken?”

sentences.text: 손님이 가방을 치워 주고, 빗소리 뒤로 기타 음악이 들려요.
sentences.translation: The customer moves their bag, and guitar music drifts in behind the sound of rain.

vocabulary.translation: moves the bag out of the way (for someone)

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 따뜻한 차 한 잔 주세요.
설탕 대신 꿀로 주세요.
여기 자리 있어요?

language_notes.title: Place a simple order
language_notes.explanation: The counter changes with the item; 잔 is used for cups or glasses of drinks.
language_notes.example: 따뜻한 라테 한 잔 주세요
language_notes.example_translation: One hot latte, please

language_notes.title: Swap one ingredient
language_notes.explanation: 대신 names what is being replaced; (으)로 marks the new choice.
language_notes.example: 우유 대신 두유로 주세요
language_notes.example_translation: Soy milk instead of milk, please

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why does Junho change his drink order?
comprehension_questions.explanation: The barista says 우유가 없어요, so Junho substitutes soy milk with 대신.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What shows that the other customer agrees to share the table?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Moving the bag clears the seat; the action answers Junho’s 자리 있어요? without extra dialogue.

sentence_building.answer: 커피 기계 소리 사이로 창가 자리 하나가 보여요.
sentence_building.translation: Through the noise of the coffee grinder, he spots one window seat.

sentence_building.answer: 창가에 앉은 손님에게 “여기 자리 있어요?”라고 물어요.
sentence_building.translation: He asks the customer by the window, “Is this seat taken?”

title: 익선동의 우산 하나
subtitle: One Umbrella in Ikseon-dong
summary: A sudden shower traps Jisoo outside a stationery shop until her neighbor appears with one small yellow umbrella.
grammar_focus: Saying you do not have something with 없어요
communicative_outcome: Say that you do not have something and offer to share.

sentences.text: 오후에 지수는 익선동 골목의 문구점에서 나와요.
sentences.translation: In the afternoon, Jisoo leaves a stationery shop in an Ikseon-dong alley.

sentences.text: 갑자기 비가 내려서 기와지붕을 크게 두드려요.
sentences.translation: Rain suddenly pours down, drumming loudly on the tiled roofs.

sentences.text: 지수는 종이 봉투는 있지만 우산이 없어요.
sentences.translation: Jisoo has a paper bag, but she does not have an umbrella.

sentences.text: 그때 같은 건물에 사는 민호가 노란 우산을 들고 와요.
sentences.translation: Just then, Minho from her building arrives with a yellow umbrella.

sentences.text: 민호는 “우산은 작지만 같이 갈까요?”라고 물어요.
sentences.translation: Minho asks, “The umbrella is small, but shall we walk together?”

sentences.text: 지수는 봉투를 품에 안고 “네, 제가 우산을 들어 줄게요”라고 해요.
sentences.translation: Holding the bag to her chest, Jisoo says, “Yes, I’ll hold the umbrella.”

sentences.text: 두 사람은 젖은 돌길을 천천히 걸어서 집에 도착해요.
sentences.translation: They walk slowly along the wet stone lane and make it home.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: I do not have an umbrella
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 오늘은 우산이 없어요.
역까지 같이 갈까요?

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: I will hold it for you
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 가방을 들어 줄게요.

language_notes.title: Say what you do not have
language_notes.explanation: Korean describes the thing as absent; the owner is often omitted when context makes it clear.
language_notes.example: 우산이 없어요
language_notes.example_translation: I do not have an umbrella

language_notes.title: Suggest doing something together
language_notes.explanation: This ending makes a soft suggestion and invites the other person’s preference.
language_notes.example: 같이 갈까요?
language_notes.example_translation: Shall we go together?

comprehension_questions.prompt: What is Jisoo trying to protect from the rain?
comprehension_questions.explanation: She has a 종이 봉투 and later holds it against her chest under the umbrella.

comprehension_questions.prompt: How does Jisoo return Minho’s help?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Minho offers to share; Jisoo answers with 제가 우산을 들어 줄게요, offering to hold it.

sentence_building.answer: 갑자기 비가 내려서 기와지붕을 크게 두드려요.
sentence_building.translation: Rain suddenly pours down, drumming loudly on the tiled roofs.

sentence_building.answer: 지수는 봉투를 품에 안고 “네, 제가 우산을 들어 줄게요”라고 해요.
sentence_building.translation: Holding the bag to her chest, Jisoo says, “Yes, I’ll hold the umbrella.”

title: 서울역의 주소
subtitle: The Address at Seoul Station
summary: Leo reaches Seoul Station with a dead phone and must show a handwritten address before he can find the right exit.
grammar_focus: Destination and location with 에 and 에서
communicative_outcome: Show an address and ask where a place is.

sentences.text: 토요일 아침, 레오는 큰 여행 가방을 끌고 서울역에 도착해요.
sentences.translation: On Saturday morning, Leo arrives at Seoul Station, pulling a large suitcase.

sentences.text: 역 안에서 빵 냄새가 나지만, 휴대전화 배터리가 다 됐어요.
sentences.translation: The station smells of fresh bread, but his phone battery is dead.

sentences.text: 레오는 종이에 쓴 숙소 주소를 역 직원에게 보여 줘요.
sentences.translation: Leo shows a station employee the guesthouse address written on a piece of paper.

sentences.text: “저기요, 이 주소로 가고 싶어요. 출구가 어디예요?”
sentences.translation: “Excuse me, I’d like to go to this address. Where is the exit?”

sentences.text: 직원은 종이를 보고 오른쪽 계단을 가리켜요.
sentences.translation: The employee reads the paper and points to the stairs on the right.

sentences.text: “출구는 저쪽이에요. 오른쪽 계단으로 올라가세요.”
sentences.translation: “The exit is over there. Check the route again once you’re outside.”

sentences.text: 레오는 “감사합니다”라고 말하고 차가운 아침 공기 속으로 나가요.
sentences.translation: Leo says, “Thank you,” and steps out into the cold morning air.

vocabulary.details: 에 marks the destination of 도착해요.

vocabulary.translation: the battery is dead / there is no battery charge

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 숙소 주소를 보여 주세요.
출구가 어디예요?
계단은 저쪽이에요.

language_notes.title: Say where you want to go
language_notes.explanation: This polite frame states your destination without sounding abrupt.
language_notes.example: 이 주소로 가고 싶어요
language_notes.example_translation: I want to go to this address
language_notes.pattern_hint: Use a destination plus:

language_notes.title: Ask for a location
language_notes.explanation: Choose 이 or 가 according to the final sound of the noun.
language_notes.example: 출구가 어디예요?
language_notes.example_translation: Where is the exit?

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why can’t Leo check the route on his phone?
comprehension_questions.explanation: The second line says 배터리가 다 됐어요, so the handwritten address becomes essential.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What does the employee’s gesture tell Leo?
choices: Use the stairs on the right
comprehension_questions.explanation: The employee points to 오른쪽 계단, the stairs on the right, before describing the exit as 저쪽.

sentence_building.answer: 역 안에서 빵 냄새가 나지만, 휴대전화 배터리가 다 됐어요.
sentence_building.translation: The station smells of fresh bread, but his phone battery is dead.

sentence_building.answer: “출구는 저쪽이에요. 오른쪽 계단으로 올라가세요.”
sentence_building.translation: “The exit is over there. Check the route again once you’re outside.”

title: 망원시장에서 덜 맵게
subtitle: Less Spicy at Mangwon Market
summary: Daniel wants to try tteokbokki at Mangwon Market, but one red spoonful sends him searching for a gentler second plate.
communicative_outcome: Order two foods and ask for a less spicy version.
target_phrases: 하나 더, 덜 맵게 해 주세요

sentences.text: 점심시간에 유나와 다니엘은 망원시장에 가요.
sentences.translation: At lunchtime, Yuna and Daniel go to Mangwon Market.

sentences.text: 가게 앞에는 참기름 냄새와 하얀 김이 가득해요.
sentences.translation: The stall is filled with the smell of sesame oil and clouds of white steam.

sentences.text: 두 사람은 “김밥하고 떡볶이 주세요”라고 말해요.
sentences.translation: They say, “Gimbap and tteokbokki, please.”

sentences.text: 다니엘은 빨간 떡볶이를 먹고 물을 바로 마셔요.
sentences.translation: Daniel tastes the bright red tteokbokki and immediately drinks some water.

sentences.text: “맛있지만 저한테는 조금 매워요.”
sentences.translation: “It’s delicious, but it’s a little spicy for me.”

sentences.text: 유나는 웃고, 다니엘은 “하나 더, 덜 맵게 해 주세요”라고 주문해요.
sentences.translation: Yuna laughs, and Daniel orders, “One more, less spicy, please.”

sentences.text: 사장님은 소스를 조금만 넣고 김밥 한 조각도 더 줘요.
sentences.translation: The vendor uses only a little sauce and adds an extra piece of gimbap.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 김밥하고 떡볶이 주세요.
이 음식은 저한테는 매워요.
소스를 덜 맵게 해 주세요.

language_notes.title: Join items in an order
language_notes.explanation: 하고 is an everyday spoken way to connect nouns in a list.
language_notes.example: 김밥하고 떡볶이 주세요
language_notes.example_translation: Gimbap and tteokbokki, please

language_notes.title: Ask for an adjustment
language_notes.explanation: This frame politely asks someone to change how something is prepared.
language_notes.example: 덜 맵게 해 주세요
language_notes.example_translation: Please make it less spicy

comprehension_questions.prompt: What makes Daniel drink water immediately?
comprehension_questions.explanation: He drinks just after tasting the red tteokbokki, then says it is 조금 매워요.

comprehension_questions.prompt: How does the vendor respond to Daniel’s second request?
choices: Uses less sauce and adds gimbap
comprehension_questions.explanation: The vendor makes the dish gentler with less sauce and adds a small extra piece of gimbap.

sentence_building.answer: 가게 앞에는 참기름 냄새와 하얀 김이 가득해요.
sentence_building.translation: The stall is filled with the smell of sesame oil and clouds of white steam.

sentence_building.answer: 유나는 웃고, 다니엘은 “하나 더, 덜 맵게 해 주세요”라고 주문해요.
sentence_building.translation: Yuna laughs, and Daniel orders, “One more, less spicy, please.”

title: 가방 밑의 교통카드
subtitle: The Card at the Bottom of the Bag
summary: Sua’s bus arrives in Gwanghwamun just as her transit card disappears beneath a notebook and a folded umbrella.
communicative_outcome: Explain that something is missing and ask when the next bus comes.

sentences.text: 수아는 광화문 근처 버스 정류장에서 파란 버스를 기다려요.
sentences.translation: Sua waits for a blue bus at a stop near Gwanghwamun.

sentences.text: 버스가 오자 수아는 가방에서 교통카드를 찾아요.
sentences.translation: When the bus arrives, Sua searches her bag for her transit card.

sentences.text: 공책과 접은 우산만 보이고 카드는 안 보여요.
sentences.translation: She can see only a notebook and a folded umbrella; the card is nowhere in sight.

sentences.text: 기사님이 문을 닫고, 버스는 젖은 길을 따라 떠나요.
sentences.translation: The driver closes the doors, and the bus pulls away along the wet road.

sentences.text: 수아는 가방 밑에서 카드를 찾았어요.
sentences.translation: Sua finds the card at the bottom of her bag.

sentences.text: 옆 사람에게 “다음 버스는 언제 와요?”라고 물어요.
sentences.translation: She asks the person beside her, “When does the next bus come?”

sentences.text: “십 분 후에 와요.” 수아는 카드를 손에 꼭 쥐어요.
sentences.translation: “In ten minutes.” Sua keeps the card clasped tightly in her hand.

vocabulary.translation: cannot be seen / is nowhere in sight

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 표가 안 보여요.
기차는 언제 와요?
십 분 후에 만나요.

language_notes.title: Say that you found something
language_notes.explanation: 찾았어요 is the polite past form of 찾다 and can mean “found” after a search.
language_notes.example: 카드를 찾았어요
language_notes.example_translation: I found the card

language_notes.title: Ask about the next arrival
language_notes.explanation: Use 다음 plus the transport noun when a departure has just been missed.
language_notes.example: 다음 버스는 언제 와요?
language_notes.example_translation: When does the next bus come?

comprehension_questions.prompt: What prevents Sua from boarding the first bus?
choices: She cannot find her transit card
She is at the wrong stop
comprehension_questions.explanation: The card is hidden under other items in her bag while the bus doors are open.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why does Sua hold the card tightly at the end?
choices: She plans to buy a new card
She does not want to lose time again
The person beside her asks for it
comprehension_questions.explanation: This is an inference: after missing one bus while searching, she makes sure the card is ready for the next one.

sentence_building.answer: 버스가 오자 수아는 가방에서 교통카드를 찾아요.
sentence_building.translation: When the bus arrives, Sua searches her bag for her transit card.

sentence_building.answer: 옆 사람에게 “다음 버스는 언제 와요?”라고 물어요.
sentence_building.translation: She asks the person beside her, “When does the next bus come?”

title: 신청서의 빈칸
subtitle: The Missing Box on the Form
summary: At a neighborhood library, Alex understands every line of the membership form except one small box marked 보호자.
communicative_outcome: Ask what a form field means and confirm what information to write.

sentences.text: 알렉스는 한국어 동화책을 빌리려고 마포구의 동네 도서관에 갔어요.
sentences.translation: Alex went to a neighborhood library in Mapo-gu to borrow Korean storybooks.

sentences.text: 안내 데스크에서 직원이 회원 신청서와 짧은 연필을 건넸어요.
sentences.translation: At the information desk, a librarian handed over a membership form and a short pencil.

sentences.text: 주소와 전화번호를 쓴 뒤, 알렉스는 “보호자”라는 단어 앞에서 멈췄어요.
sentences.translation: After writing an address and phone number, Alex stopped at the word 보호자.

sentences.text: “이 단어는 무슨 뜻이에요? 여기에는 뭘 쓰면 돼요?”
sentences.translation: “What does this word mean? What should I write here?”

sentences.text: 직원은 “어린이에게 필요한 항목이에요. 이 칸은 비워 두셔도 돼요”라고 설명했어요.
sentences.translation: The librarian explained, “That field is for children. You may leave this box blank.”

sentences.text: 카드가 나오자 작은 기계에서 맑은 알림음이 났어요.
sentences.translation: When the card printed, a clear chime sounded from the little machine.

sentences.text: 알렉스는 비닐 표지가 반짝이는 짧은 동화책 두 권을 골랐어요.
sentences.translation: Alex chose two short storybooks with shiny plastic covers.

sentences.text: 이번에는 직원의 도움 없이 직접 대출하고 카드를 지갑에 넣었어요.
sentences.translation: This time, Alex checked them out without help and slipped the card into a wallet.

vocabulary.details: A guardian field may apply to a child rather than an adult applicant.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 이 표현은 무슨 뜻이에요?
이 칸에는 뭘 쓰면 돼요?
두 번째 줄은 비워 두셔도 돼요.
도움 없이 신청했어요.

language_notes.title: Ask what action is enough
language_notes.explanation: The pattern asks for the action that will satisfy a requirement.
language_notes.example: 여기에는 뭘 쓰면 돼요?
language_notes.example_translation: What should I write here?

language_notes.title: Give permission to leave something blank
language_notes.explanation: The honorific 시 inside -(으)셔도 돼요 politely gives permission to a customer.
language_notes.example: 이 칸은 비워 두셔도 돼요
language_notes.example_translation: You may leave this box blank

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why can Alex leave the 보호자 box empty?
choices: The field is only for children
The address is enough for every applicant
comprehension_questions.explanation: The librarian identifies it as 어린이에게 필요한 항목, a field needed for children.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What shows Alex has become more independent by the end?
choices: Alex checks out the books without help
Alex asks for a second form
comprehension_questions.explanation: The final line contrasts the earlier explanation with 직접 대출하고, completing the checkout independently.

sentence_building.answer: 안내 데스크에서 직원이 회원 신청서와 짧은 연필을 건넸어요.
sentence_building.translation: At the information desk, a librarian handed over a membership form and a short pencil.

sentence_building.answer: 알렉스는 비닐 표지가 반짝이는 짧은 동화책 두 권을 골랐어요.
sentence_building.translation: Alex chose two short storybooks with shiny plastic covers.

title: 현관 옆의 신발
subtitle: Shoes by the Door
summary: Nari plans a quiet birthday dinner in Daejeon, but unfamiliar silence and three pairs of shoes betray her friends’ secret.
communicative_outcome: Describe an intention, notice evidence, and react to a surprise.

sentences.text: 나리는 생일 저녁을 대전의 집에서 조용히 보내려고 했어요.
sentences.translation: Nari planned to spend her birthday evening quietly at home in Daejeon.

sentences.text: 퇴근길에 작은 딸기 팩과 미역국 재료만 사서 현관문을 열었어요.
sentences.translation: On the way home, she bought only a small pack of strawberries and ingredients for seaweed soup.

sentences.text: 거실은 이상할 만큼 조용했고 부엌 불도 꺼져 있었어요.
sentences.translation: The living room was strangely quiet, and the kitchen light was off.

sentences.text: 불을 켜려고 하는데 현관 옆에 친구들의 신발 세 켤레가 보였어요.
sentences.translation: As she reached for the light, she saw three pairs of her friends’ shoes by the door.

sentences.text: 나리는 웃음을 참으며 아무것도 모르는 척 부엌으로 들어갔어요.
sentences.translation: Holding back a laugh, Nari walked into the kitchen and pretended not to know.

sentences.text: 갑자기 불이 켜지고 친구들이 작은 케이크와 따뜻한 미역국을 들고 나왔어요.
sentences.translation: Suddenly the lights came on, and her friends appeared with a small cake and warm seaweed soup.

sentences.text: 혜진이 “큰 파티 싫어하니까 우리끼리만 준비했어. 그런데 어떻게 알았어?”라고 물었어요.
sentences.translation: Hyejin said, “You don’t like big parties, so we kept it to just us. But how did you know?”

sentences.text: 나리는 대답 대신 문 옆의 신발을 가리키며 먼저 웃었어요.
sentences.translation: Instead of answering, Nari pointed at the shoes by the door and laughed first.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 집에서 쉬려고 했어요.
신발 세 켤레가 있어요.
선물을 보고도 모르는 척했어요.
오늘은 우리끼리 저녁을 먹어요.

language_notes.title: Talk about a plan that changed
language_notes.explanation: The past 했어요 often implies that the original intention met a change or interruption.
language_notes.example: 집에서 조용히 보내려고 했어요
language_notes.example_translation: I planned to spend it quietly at home

language_notes.title: Set up an interruption
language_notes.explanation: -는데 holds the first action open while the next detail changes the scene.
language_notes.example: 불을 켜려고 하는데 현관 옆에 친구들의 신발 세 켤레가 보였어요
language_notes.example_translation: As she was about to turn on the light, she saw three pairs of her friends’ shoes

comprehension_questions.prompt: What reveals the surprise before Nari enters the kitchen?
comprehension_questions.explanation: The shoes by the entryway are physical evidence that her friends are already inside.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why do the friends keep the celebration small?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Hyejin says 큰 파티 싫어하니까, showing that the scale reflects Nari’s preference.

sentence_building.answer: 퇴근길에 작은 딸기 팩과 미역국 재료만 사서 현관문을 열었어요.
sentence_building.translation: On the way home, she bought only a small pack of strawberries and ingredients for seaweed soup.

sentence_building.answer: 혜진이 “큰 파티 싫어하니까 우리끼리만 준비했어. 그런데 어떻게 알았어?”라고 물었어요.
sentence_building.translation: Hyejin said, “You don’t like big parties, so we kept it to just us. But how did you know?”

title: 마지막 환승
subtitle: The Last Transfer
summary: A delayed last train gives Taeho five unexpected minutes to help an older passenger untangle her route home.
communicative_outcome: Ask a destination respectfully and explain where to transfer.
target_phrases: 제가 같은 방향이라 공덕역까지 같이 갈게요

sentences.text: 태호는 야근을 마치고 마지막 전철을 타려고 을지로의 역으로 뛰어갔어요.
sentences.translation: After working late, Taeho ran to a station in Euljiro to catch the last train.

sentences.text: 전광판에는 전철이 오 분 늦게 온다는 안내가 떠 있었어요.
sentences.translation: The display showed that the train would arrive five minutes late.

sentences.text: 기다리는 동안 옆에 있던 어르신이 접힌 노선도를 여러 번 돌려 보셨어요.
sentences.translation: While he waited, an older passenger beside him kept turning a folded route map around.

sentences.text: 태호는 “어디까지 가세요?”라고 조심스럽게 물었어요.
sentences.translation: Taeho carefully asked, “Where are you headed?”

sentences.text: 목적지를 들은 뒤 “공덕역에서 갈아타시면 돼요”라고 노선 위를 짚어 드렸어요.
sentences.translation: After hearing the destination, he traced the line and said, “You can transfer at Gongdeok Station.”

sentences.text: 어르신은 막차라서 환승을 놓칠까 봐 걱정했다고 하셨어요.
sentences.translation: The passenger said they had been worried about missing the transfer because it was the last train.

sentences.text: 태호는 “제가 같은 방향이라 공덕역까지 같이 갈게요”라고 말했어요.
sentences.translation: Taeho said, “I’m going the same way, so I’ll ride with you as far as Gongdeok.”

sentences.text: 전철 불빛이 터널에 나타나자, 두 사람은 같은 문 앞에 나란히 섰어요.
sentences.translation: When the train lights appeared in the tunnel, they stood side by side at the same door.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 기다리는 동안 노선도를 봤어요.
오늘 어디까지 가세요?
다음 역에서 갈아타시면 돼요.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: I worried I might be late
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 늦을까 봐 걱정했어요.

language_notes.title: Place one action inside another
language_notes.explanation: The 동안 clause provides the span of time in which the main event happens.
language_notes.example: 기다리는 동안 옆에 있던 어르신이 접힌 노선도를 여러 번 돌려 보셨어요
language_notes.example_translation: While he waited, an older passenger beside him kept turning a folded route map around

language_notes.title: Give a respectful route instruction
language_notes.explanation: Adding 시 makes the instruction respectful toward the older passenger.
language_notes.example: 공덕역에서 갈아타시면 돼요
language_notes.example_translation: You can transfer at Gongdeok Station

comprehension_questions.prompt: What first suggests that the older passenger needs help?
choices: They repeatedly turn the route map around
They stand on the wrong platform
comprehension_questions.explanation: The repeated movement of the folded map is a visual clue before Taeho asks any question.

comprehension_questions.prompt: How does Taeho reduce the passenger’s worry about the last transfer?
choices: He offers to travel together to Gongdeok
He asks the train to wait
comprehension_questions.explanation: Because he is going the same way, Taeho offers concrete help through the transfer point.

sentence_building.answer: 전광판에는 전철이 오 분 늦게 온다는 안내가 떠 있었어요.
sentence_building.translation: The display showed that the train would arrive five minutes late.

sentence_building.answer: 태호는 “제가 같은 방향이라 공덕역까지 같이 갈게요”라고 말했어요.
sentence_building.translation: Taeho said, “I’m going the same way, so I’ll ride with you as far as Gongdeok.”

title: 검은 우산 두 개
subtitle: Two Black Umbrellas
summary: Hana leaves a Seongsu café with the wrong black umbrella, then returns to find its owner protecting hers from the rain.
communicative_outcome: Explain a mix-up, apologize, and return an item.

sentences.text: 하나는 성수동 카페에서 공부를 마치고 나서 밖으로 나왔어요.
sentences.translation: After finishing her work at a café in Seongsu-dong, Hana stepped outside.

sentences.text: 비가 유리창을 두드렸고, 우산꽂이에는 검은 우산 하나만 남아 있었어요.
sentences.translation: Rain tapped the factory windows, and only one black umbrella remained in the stand.

sentences.text: 하나는 제 우산인 줄 알고 들고 나갔어요.
sentences.translation: Hana picked it up, thinking it was hers.

sentences.text: 횡단보도 앞에서 손잡이에 달린 파란 이름표를 발견했어요.
sentences.translation: At the crosswalk, she noticed a blue name tag tied to the handle.

sentences.text: 이름표에는 “도윤”이라고 적혀 있어서 하나는 곧바로 카페로 돌아갔어요.
sentences.translation: The tag read “Doyun,” so Hana went straight back to the café.

sentences.text: “죄송해요. 제 우산인 줄 알았어요. 바로 돌려드릴게요.”
sentences.translation: “I’m sorry. I thought it was mine. Let me give it back.”

sentences.text: 도윤은 하나의 줄무늬 우산을 내밀며 “괜찮아요. 저도 바뀐 줄 알았어요”라고 했어요.
sentences.translation: Holding out Hana’s striped umbrella, Doyun said, “It’s okay. I thought they’d been switched too.”

sentences.text: 두 사람은 젖은 우산을 바꾸고, 이번에는 이름표를 확인한 뒤 웃었어요.
sentences.translation: They exchanged the dripping umbrellas and laughed after checking the tags this time.

vocabulary.translation: I will return it to you (honorific)

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: I thought it was my bag
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 제 가방인 줄 알았어요.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: went straight back to the shop
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 가게로 곧바로 돌아갔어요.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: I will return it to you
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 내일 책을 돌려드릴게요.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: I thought they had been switched
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 표가 바뀐 줄 알았어요.

language_notes.title: Correct a mistaken assumption
language_notes.explanation: Use this after discovering that what you believed was not true.
language_notes.example: 제 우산인 줄 알았어요
language_notes.example_translation: I thought it was my umbrella

language_notes.title: Promise to return something politely
language_notes.explanation: 드리다 adds respect toward the person receiving the returned item.
language_notes.example: 바로 돌려드릴게요
language_notes.example_translation: I’ll return it right away

comprehension_questions.prompt: What proves that the black umbrella is not Hana’s?
comprehension_questions.explanation: The name 도윤 on the blue tag overturns Hana’s assumption that the umbrella is hers.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why is Doyun already holding Hana’s striped umbrella?
choices: He also noticed the umbrellas were switched
The barista gave it to him as a gift
comprehension_questions.explanation: His line 저도 바뀐 줄 알았어요 shows that he independently understood the same mix-up.

sentence_building.answer: 비가 유리창을 두드렸고, 우산꽂이에는 검은 우산 하나만 남아 있었어요.
sentence_building.translation: Rain tapped the factory windows, and only one black umbrella remained in the stand.

sentence_building.answer: 도윤은 하나의 줄무늬 우산을 내밀며 “괜찮아요. 저도 바뀐 줄 알았어요”라고 했어요.
sentence_building.translation: Holding out Hana’s striped umbrella, Doyun said, “It’s okay. I thought they’d been switched too.”

title: 북한산의 마른 길
subtitle: The Dry Path on Bukhansan
summary: After overnight rain, Mira and Sunwoo must choose between the familiar muddy trail and a longer route recommended by a ranger.
setting_tags: A Bukhansan trail on a Saturday morning
communicative_outcome: Give a reason, suggest a safer option, and agree on a route.
target_phrases: 위쪽 길이 미끄러우니까 오른쪽 길로 가세요

sentences.text: 토요일 아침, 미라와 선우는 북한산 입구에서 등산화를 단단히 묶었어요.
sentences.translation: On Saturday morning, Mira and Sunwoo tightened their hiking boots at the entrance to Bukhansan.

sentences.text: 밤새 비가 내려서 돌계단과 솔잎이 검게 젖어 있었어요.
sentences.translation: Overnight rain had left the stone steps and pine needles dark and wet.

sentences.text: 안내소 직원은 “위쪽 길이 미끄러우니까 오른쪽 길로 가세요”라고 말했어요.
sentences.translation: A ranger said, “The upper trail is slippery, so take the path on the right.”

sentences.text: 선우는 평소에 가던 길을 보며 “조금만 조심하면 괜찮지 않을까?”라고 물었어요.
sentences.translation: Looking toward their usual trail, Sunwoo asked, “Wouldn’t it be fine if we were just careful?”

sentences.text: 미라는 젖은 바위를 가리키며 “조금 멀어도 안전한 길로 가는 게 어때?”라고 했어요.
sentences.translation: Pointing at the wet rocks, Mira said, “How about taking the safer path, even if it’s a little longer?”

sentences.text: 두 사람은 오른쪽 길을 골라서 서두르지 않고 천천히 올라갔어요.
sentences.translation: They chose the right-hand trail and climbed without rushing.

sentences.text: 낮은 전망대에 도착하자 구름 사이로 서울의 지붕들이 보였어요.
sentences.translation: At a low lookout, Seoul’s rooftops appeared between the clouds.

sentences.text: 선우는 보리차를 따르며 “천천히 오니까 이런 곳도 보네”라고 웃었어요.
sentences.translation: Pouring barley tea, Sunwoo laughed. “Coming slowly means we get to see a place like this.”

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 바닥이 미끄러우니까 조심하세요.
지하철로 가는 게 어때요?

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: even if it is a little far
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: 조금 멀어도 걸어가요.
서두르지 않고 천천히 하세요.

language_notes.title: Give a reason for advice
language_notes.explanation: This connective presents a reason that supports what the speaker recommends next.
language_notes.example: 위쪽 길이 미끄러우니까 오른쪽 길로 가세요
language_notes.example_translation: The upper trail is slippery, so take the path on the right

language_notes.title: Offer an alternative
language_notes.explanation: Drop 요 only with someone close enough for casual speech, as Mira does with her friend.
language_notes.example: 안전한 길로 가는 게 어때?
language_notes.example_translation: How about taking the safer path?

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why does the ranger recommend the right-hand trail?
comprehension_questions.explanation: 미끄러우니까 directly links the wet upper trail to the safer route recommendation.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What unexpected benefit comes from choosing the longer route?
choices: They find a quiet lookout view
comprehension_questions.explanation: The slower route leads to a lower lookout where the city rooftops appear between clouds.

sentence_building.answer: 밤새 비가 내려서 돌계단과 솔잎이 검게 젖어 있었어요.
sentence_building.translation: Overnight rain had left the stone steps and pine needles dark and wet.

sentence_building.answer: 낮은 전망대에 도착하자 구름 사이로 서울의 지붕들이 보였어요.
sentence_building.translation: At a low lookout, Seoul’s rooftops appeared between the clouds.

title: Красная варежка на снегу
subtitle: The Red Mitten in the Snow
summary: On the first snowy morning in Yekaterinburg, Lena follows a trail of small footprints to return a child’s red mitten.
setting_tags: A residential street in Yekaterinburg after the first snow
grammar_focus: Location with на and ownership with ваш/ваша
communicative_outcome: Describe where an object is and ask whether it belongs to someone.
target_phrases: На свежем снегу лежит маленькая красная варежка

sentences.text: Утром Лена идёт на работу по тихой улице Екатеринбурга. Холодный воздух пахнет совсем свежим снегом.
sentences.translation: In the morning, Lena walks to work along a quiet street in Yekaterinburg. The cold air smells of brand-new snow.

sentences.text: На свежем снегу лежит маленькая красная варежка.
sentences.translation: A small red mitten lies on the fresh snow.

sentences.text: Рядом видны детские следы, которые ведут к трамвайной остановке.
sentences.translation: Nearby, a child’s footprints lead toward the tram stop.

sentences.text: Лена берёт варежку и слышит впереди звон трамвая.
sentences.translation: Lena picks up the mitten and hears a tram bell ahead.

sentences.text: У остановки отец надевает ребёнку только одну варежку.
sentences.translation: At the stop, a father is putting only one mitten on his child.

sentences.text: Лена спрашивает: «Извините, это ваша варежка?»
sentences.translation: Lena asks, “Excuse me, is this your mitten?”

sentences.text: Отец улыбается: «Да, спасибо! Мы её искали».
sentences.translation: The father smiles. “Yes, thank you! We were looking for it.”

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: A scarf lies on the snow
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: На снегу лежит шарф.
Это ваша сумка?
Спасибо, мы её искали.

language_notes.title: Locate an object in a scene
language_notes.explanation: Russian often puts the location first when introducing a new object.
language_notes.example: На свежем снегу лежит маленькая красная варежка
language_notes.example_translation: A small red mitten lies on the fresh snow

language_notes.title: Check whether something belongs to someone
language_notes.explanation: Match ваш to the noun’s grammatical gender: варежка is feminine, so the form is ваша.
language_notes.example: это ваша варежка?
language_notes.example_translation: Is this your mitten?

comprehension_questions.prompt: What clue helps Lena find the mitten’s owner?
comprehension_questions.explanation: The детские следы lead from the mitten toward the stop where a child has only one mitten.

comprehension_questions.prompt: How does Lena confirm ownership?
choices: She asks whether it is theirs
comprehension_questions.explanation: Это ваша варежка? is a direct but polite ownership check with an unfamiliar adult.

sentence_building.answer: На свежем снегу лежит маленькая красная варежка.
sentence_building.translation: A small red mitten lies on the fresh snow.

sentence_building.answer: Лена спрашивает: «Извините, это ваша варежка?»
sentence_building.translation: Lena asks, “Excuse me, is this your mitten?”

title: Нет соли для помидоров
subtitle: No Salt for the Tomatoes
summary: At a Sunday lunch outside Tula, a bowl of garden tomatoes is ready before anyone notices the empty salt jar.
grammar_focus: Absence with нет and the genitive
communicative_outcome: Say that something is missing and ask a neighbor to lend a small amount.

sentences.text: В воскресенье Лена и Миша готовят обед на даче под Тулой.
sentences.translation: On Sunday, Lena and Misha prepare lunch at their dacha outside Tula.

sentences.text: На деревянном столе лежат тёплые помидоры, огурцы и свежий укроп.
sentences.translation: Sun-warmed tomatoes, cucumbers, and fresh dill lie on the wooden table.

sentences.text: Лена режет салат, а Миша открывает шкаф и находит пустую банку.
sentences.translation: Lena chops the salad while Misha opens the cupboard and finds an empty jar.

sentences.text: «У нас нет соли», — говорит он.
sentences.translation: “We don’t have any salt,” he says.

sentences.text: Лена идёт к соседке Вере: «Можно немного соли для салата?»
sentences.translation: Lena goes to their neighbor Vera. “Could we have a little salt for the salad?”

sentences.text: Вера отвечает: «Конечно. Я сейчас принесу. А вам нужны ещё яблоки?»
sentences.translation: Vera answers, “Of course. I’ll bring some now. Do you need more apples too?”

sentences.text: Лена возвращается с солью и тремя зелёными яблоками, а калитка тихо скрипит.
sentences.translation: Lena returns with salt and three green apples as the garden gate creaks softly.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: We do not have any bread
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: У нас нет хлеба.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: Could I have a little water?
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Можно немного воды?

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: I will bring it right now
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Подождите, я сейчас принесу соль.

language_notes.title: Say that something is missing
language_notes.explanation: After нет, the missing thing takes the genitive case: соль becomes соли.
language_notes.example: У нас нет соли
language_notes.example_translation: We do not have any salt

language_notes.title: Ask for a small amount
language_notes.explanation: Немного also governs the genitive and softens a request for an uncounted amount.
language_notes.example: Можно немного соли для салата?
language_notes.example_translation: Could we have a little salt for the salad?

comprehension_questions.prompt: What is missing from the lunch table?
comprehension_questions.explanation: The jar is empty, and Misha says У нас нет соли, using the genitive after нет.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What extra item does Vera send back with Lena?
comprehension_questions.explanation: The final line adds three green apples, turning a borrowed ingredient into a small neighborly exchange.

sentence_building.answer: На деревянном столе лежат тёплые помидоры, огурцы и свежий укроп.
sentence_building.translation: Sun-warmed tomatoes, cucumbers, and fresh dill lie on the wooden table.

sentence_building.answer: Вера отвечает: «Конечно. Я сейчас принесу. А вам нужны ещё яблоки?»
sentence_building.translation: Vera answers, “Of course. I’ll bring some now. Do you need more apples too?”

title: Последняя булочка с корицей
subtitle: The Last Cinnamon Bun
summary: Anna reaches a bakery on Vasilyevsky Island just as another customer buys the cinnamon bun she came for.
setting_tags: A neighborhood bakery on Vasilyevsky Island, Saint Petersburg
grammar_focus: Accusative objects in a simple order
communicative_outcome: Ask what is still available and order one pastry with tea.
target_phrases: Один пирожок с яблоком и чай, пожалуйста

sentences.text: В субботу утром Анна заходит в маленькую пекарню на Васильевском острове.
sentences.translation: On Saturday morning, Anna steps into a small bakery on Vasilyevsky Island.

sentences.text: Внутри пахнет ржаным хлебом и корицей, а окна запотели от тепла.
sentences.translation: Inside, the air smells of rye bread and cinnamon, and the windows are fogged with warmth.

sentences.text: Покупатель перед Анной берёт последнюю булочку с корицей.
sentences.translation: The customer ahead of Anna takes the last cinnamon bun.

sentences.text: Анна вздыхает и спрашивает продавщицу: «А что ещё тёплое есть?»
sentences.translation: Anna sighs and asks the clerk, “What else do you have that’s warm?”

sentences.text: «Один пирожок с яблоком и чай, пожалуйста».
sentences.translation: “One apple pastry and tea, please.”

sentences.text: Продавщица кладёт горячий пирожок на синюю тарелку.
sentences.translation: The clerk places the hot pastry on a blue plate.

sentences.text: Анна садится у окна, слышит хруст теста и улыбается: новый выбор ей нравится.
sentences.translation: Anna sits by the window, hears the pastry crackle, and smiles: she likes her new choice.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Кофе нет. А что ещё есть?
Один пирожок с яблоком, пожалуйста.
Можно сесть у окна?

language_notes.title: Order one item
language_notes.explanation: The number changes with gender and quantity: один пирожок, одну булочку, два чая.
language_notes.example: Один пирожок с яблоком и чай, пожалуйста
language_notes.example_translation: One apple pastry and tea, please

language_notes.title: Ask for another option
language_notes.explanation: The phrase keeps the conversation moving after your first choice is unavailable.
language_notes.example: А что ещё тёплое есть?
language_notes.example_translation: What else do you have that’s warm?
variants: А что ещё без сахара есть?

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why does Anna change her order?
choices: Another customer takes the last cinnamon bun
comprehension_questions.explanation: Последнюю булочку means “the last bun,” so Anna must ask what else is warm.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What suggests that Anna enjoys the replacement?
choices: She smiles at the pastry’s crisp sound
comprehension_questions.explanation: The final line joins the хруст, or crisp crackle, with her smile and explicit approval.

sentence_building.answer: Внутри пахнет ржаным хлебом и корицей, а окна запотели от тепла.
sentence_building.translation: Inside, the air smells of rye bread and cinnamon, and the windows are fogged with warmth.

sentence_building.answer: Продавщица кладёт горячий пирожок на синюю тарелку.
sentence_building.translation: The clerk places the hot pastry on a blue plate.

title: Карта у Ленинградского вокзала
subtitle: The Card at Leningradsky Station
summary: Maria arrives in Moscow with a suitcase and coins, but the metro machine offers more ticket choices than she expected.
setting_tags: The metro entrance near Leningradsky Station, Moscow
grammar_focus: Asking where with где and an infinitive
communicative_outcome: Ask where to buy a transit card and confirm the correct machine.

sentences.text: Мария выходит с Ленинградского вокзала с маленьким чемоданом.
sentences.translation: Maria leaves Leningradsky Station with a small suitcase.

sentences.text: У входа в метро громко звучат объявления, и люди спешат к турникетам.
sentences.translation: Announcements echo at the metro entrance as people hurry toward the gates.

sentences.text: На экране автомата Мария видит много разных билетов.
sentences.translation: On the machine’s screen, Maria sees many different tickets.

sentences.text: Она подходит к сотруднику: «Подскажите, пожалуйста, где купить карту?»
sentences.translation: She approaches an employee. “Could you tell me where to buy a card, please?”

sentences.text: Сотрудник показывает на соседний автомат: «Вот здесь. Нажмите синюю кнопку».
sentences.translation: The employee points to the next machine. “Right here. Press the blue button.”

sentences.text: Мария уточняет: «Этот автомат принимает банковские карты?»
sentences.translation: Maria checks, “Does this machine accept bank cards?”

sentences.text: Через минуту новая карта лежит у неё в ладони, и турникет открывается.
sentences.translation: A minute later, the new card rests in her palm and the gate opens.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Подскажите, пожалуйста, где метро.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: Where can I buy a ticket?
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Где купить билет?
Извините, этот автомат работает?

language_notes.title: Open a polite request for information
language_notes.explanation: Подскажите softens a practical question to a stranger or employee.
language_notes.example: Подскажите, пожалуйста, где купить карту?
language_notes.example_translation: Could you tell me where to buy a card, please?

language_notes.title: Confirm the machine you mean
language_notes.explanation: Match этот, эта, or это to the grammatical gender of the noun.
language_notes.example: Этот автомат принимает банковские карты?
language_notes.example_translation: Does this machine accept bank cards?

comprehension_questions.prompt: What confuses Maria at first?
choices: The screen shows many ticket choices
comprehension_questions.explanation: The many ticket options on the machine lead her to ask a staff member where to buy the card.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What does Maria verify before paying?
choices: Whether the machine accepts bank cards
comprehension_questions.explanation: Her follow-up uses этот автомат to confirm the payment method for the specific machine.

sentence_building.answer: У входа в метро громко звучат объявления, и люди спешат к турникетам.
sentence_building.translation: Announcements echo at the metro entrance as people hurry toward the gates.

sentence_building.answer: Мария уточняет: «Этот автомат принимает банковские карты?»
sentence_building.translation: Maria checks, “Does this machine accept bank cards?”

title: Ключ не поворачивается
subtitle: A Key That Will Not Turn
summary: Pavel’s first evening in a Kazan apartment begins with a basil plant, two heavy bags, and a stubborn front-door key.
communicative_outcome: Introduce yourself, explain a simple problem, and accept help.

sentences.text: Вечером Павел поднимается на третий этаж с двумя сумками и горшком базилика.
sentences.translation: In the evening, Pavel climbs to the third floor with two bags and a pot of basil.

sentences.text: Он вставляет ключ в дверь новой квартиры, но ключ не поворачивается.
sentences.translation: He puts the key into his new apartment door, but it will not turn.

sentences.text: Из соседней двери выходит Ольга, и Павел говорит: «Здравствуйте. Я ваш новый сосед».
sentences.translation: Olga steps out of the next apartment, and Pavel says, “Hello. I’m your new neighbor.”

sentences.text: «У меня не открывается дверь. Здесь есть секрет?»
sentences.translation: “My door won’t open. Is there a trick to it?”

sentences.text: Ольга улыбается: «Нужно немного поднять ручку. Давайте попробуем вместе».
sentences.translation: Olga smiles. “You need to lift the handle a little. Let’s try together.”

sentences.text: Дверь открывается, и по лестнице сразу пахнет свежим базиликом.
sentences.translation: The door opens, and the stairwell suddenly smells of fresh basil.

sentences.text: Павел обещает после переезда зайти к Ольге на чай.
sentences.translation: Pavel promises to stop by for tea once he has unpacked.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Здравствуйте, я ваш новый сосед.
У меня не открывается дверь.
Давайте ещё раз попробуем вместе.

language_notes.title: Describe a problem you have
language_notes.explanation: Russian often frames a personal situation with у меня rather than a possessive adjective.
language_notes.example: У меня не открывается дверь
language_notes.example_translation: My door won’t open

language_notes.title: Suggest solving something together
language_notes.explanation: Давайте makes a cooperative suggestion and fits polite вы-register.
language_notes.example: Давайте попробуем вместе
language_notes.example_translation: Let’s try together

comprehension_questions.prompt: What prevents Pavel from entering his apartment?
choices: He is on the wrong floor
comprehension_questions.explanation: The key fits the lock but не поворачивается, so the difficulty is the handle technique.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What future invitation grows out of Olga’s help?
comprehension_questions.explanation: The practical first meeting ends with Pavel promising to visit Olga for tea after the move.

sentence_building.answer: Он вставляет ключ в дверь новой квартиры, но ключ не поворачивается.
sentence_building.translation: He puts the key into his new apartment door, but it will not turn.

sentence_building.answer: Дверь открывается, и по лестнице сразу пахнет свежим базиликом.
sentence_building.translation: The door opens, and the stairwell suddenly smells of fresh basil.

title: Все в одном экране
subtitle: Everyone in One Screen
summary: Olga comes home late on her birthday expecting one quiet call, but her brother fits the whole family into the frame.
grammar_focus: Purpose with чтобы and an infinitive
communicative_outcome: Explain a purpose and describe an event that happened earlier than planned.
target_phrases: Ольга как раз собиралась звонить маме
Мы все собрались у мамы, чтобы поздравить тебя вместе

sentences.text: В день рождения Ольга вернулась в свою квартиру в Екатеринбурге позже обычного.
sentences.translation: On her birthday, Olga returned to her apartment in Yekaterinburg later than usual.

sentences.text: Она поставила чайник и достала из холодильника маленький кусок медовика. В квартире было совсем тихо и пусто.
sentences.translation: She put the kettle on and took a small slice of honey cake from the fridge. The apartment was completely quiet and empty.

sentences.text: Ольга как раз собиралась звонить маме, когда первой зазвонил её телефон.
sentences.translation: Olga was just about to call her mother when her own phone rang first.

sentences.text: На экране появилось лицо брата, а за ним сразу несколько знакомых голосов.
sentences.translation: Her brother’s face appeared on the screen, followed by several familiar voices at once.

sentences.text: Брат отодвинул телефон, и Ольга увидела маму, тётю и двух двоюродных сестёр.
sentences.translation: Her brother moved the phone back, and Olga saw her mother, aunt, and two cousins.

sentences.text: «Мы все собрались у мамы, чтобы поздравить тебя вместе», — объяснил он.
sentences.translation: “We all gathered at Mom’s so we could wish you happy birthday together,” he explained.

sentences.text: Ольга засмеялась: «Подождите, я тоже зажгу свечу, и тогда начинайте».
sentences.translation: Olga laughed. “Wait, I’ll light a candle too, and then you can begin.”

sentences.text: Через минуту один огонёк дрожал перед камерой, а вся семья пела немного не в такт.
sentences.translation: A minute later, one flame flickered before the camera while the whole family sang slightly out of time.

vocabulary.translation: in order to congratulate / wish happy birthday

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Я как раз собиралась тебе звонить.
Мы позвонили, чтобы поздравить тебя.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: Wait, I will get some tea too
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Подождите, я тоже возьму чай.
Мы пели немного не в такт.

language_notes.title: Explain why people gathered
language_notes.explanation: Чтобы introduces the purpose of the action in the first clause.
language_notes.example: Мы все собрались у мамы, чтобы поздравить тебя вместе
language_notes.example_translation: We all gathered at Mom’s so we could wish you happy birthday together

language_notes.title: Say you were about to do something
language_notes.explanation: Как раз makes the timing immediate: the planned action was about to happen.
language_notes.example: Ольга как раз собиралась звонить маме
language_notes.example_translation: Olga was just about to call her mother

comprehension_questions.prompt: What had Olga planned to do before the incoming call?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Как раз собиралась звонить marks the action Olga was on the point of starting.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why has the family gathered at Olga’s mother’s home?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Чтобы поздравить states the family’s shared purpose directly.

sentence_building.answer: Она поставила чайник и достала из холодильника маленький кусок медовика. В квартире было совсем тихо и пусто.
sentence_building.translation: She put the kettle on and took a small slice of honey cake from the fridge. The apartment was completely quiet and empty.

sentence_building.answer: Ольга засмеялась: «Подождите, я тоже зажгу свечу, и тогда начинайте».
sentence_building.translation: Olga laughed. “Wait, I’ll light a candle too, and then you can begin.”

title: Звонок под ступеньками
subtitle: The Bell Beneath the Steps
summary: When a familiar courtyard cat disappears in Kazan, three neighbors compare what they heard before opening the basement grille.
grammar_focus: Relative clauses with который and которого
communicative_outcome: Describe a familiar animal, compare clues, and explain when something finally happened.
target_phrases: когда они видели Барсика в последний раз
Барсик вышел только тогда, когда Галина постучала ложкой по металлической миске

sentences.text: Во дворе казанского дома жил рыжий кот Барсик, которого знали все соседи.
sentences.translation: An orange cat named Barsik lived in the courtyard of a Kazan apartment building, and every neighbor knew him.

sentences.text: Обычно он ждал завтрака у подъезда рядом с велосипедами, но во вторник его миска осталась полной.
sentences.translation: He usually waited for breakfast beside the bicycles at the entrance, but on Tuesday his bowl remained full.

sentences.text: Саша спросил соседей, когда они видели Барсика в последний раз.
sentences.translation: Sasha asked the neighbors when they had last seen Barsik.

sentences.text: Галина слышала тихий звон его ошейника под ступеньками, а Тимур заметил следы у подвальной решётки.
sentences.translation: Galina had heard the faint bell on his collar beneath the steps, while Timur had noticed tracks by the basement grille.

sentences.text: Дворник открыл решётку, и из темноты пахнуло пылью и сырой землёй.
sentences.translation: The caretaker opened the grille, and the dark space breathed out dust and damp earth.

sentences.text: Саша позвал кота, но в ответ услышал только короткое мяуканье.
sentences.translation: Sasha called the cat, but only a short meow answered.

sentences.text: Барсик вышел только тогда, когда Галина постучала ложкой по металлической миске.
sentences.translation: Barsik came out only when Galina tapped a spoon against the metal bowl.

sentences.text: На следующее утро кот снова сидел у подъезда, а рядом лежала записка: «Решётку закрывайте осторожно».
sentences.translation: The next morning, the cat was back by the entrance beside a note: “Please close the grille carefully.”

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: the cat whom the neighbors feed
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Это кот, которого кормят соседи.
Когда вы видели его в последний раз?

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: In reply I heard a meow
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: В ответ я услышал мяуканье.
Он вышел только тогда, когда услышал миску.

language_notes.title: Describe an animate masculine noun
language_notes.explanation: Которого is accusative here because the known person or animal is animate and receives the action.
language_notes.example: рыжий кот Барсик, которого знали все соседи
language_notes.example_translation: an orange cat named Barsik, whom every neighbor knew

language_notes.title: Name the condition that finally worked
language_notes.explanation: The frame emphasizes that earlier attempts failed and this condition changed the result.
language_notes.example: Барсик вышел только тогда, когда Галина постучала ложкой по металлической миске
language_notes.example_translation: Barsik came out only when Galina tapped a spoon against the metal bowl
variants: Он ответил только тогда, когда я позвонил
Дверь открылась только тогда, когда пришёл дворник
Кот подошёл только тогда, когда услышал миску

comprehension_questions.prompt: Which two clues point toward the basement grille?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Galina hears the bell beneath the steps, and Timur sees tracks beside the grille.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What finally persuades Barsik to come out?
choices: A spoon tapping his metal bowl
comprehension_questions.explanation: Только тогда, когда marks the bowl sound as the condition that succeeds after calling fails.

sentence_building.answer: Обычно он ждал завтрака у подъезда рядом с велосипедами, но во вторник его миска осталась полной.
sentence_building.translation: He usually waited for breakfast beside the bicycles at the entrance, but on Tuesday his bowl remained full.

sentence_building.answer: Барсик вышел только тогда, когда Галина постучала ложкой по металлической миске.
sentence_building.translation: Barsik came out only when Galina tapped a spoon against the metal bowl.

title: Чек в кармане пальто
subtitle: The Receipt in the Coat Pocket
summary: Nina notices her gloves are missing only after a cold tram ride, and a café receipt becomes the first step back to them.
setting_tags: A café and tram route in central Saint Petersburg
grammar_focus: Past motion verbs and retracing a route
communicative_outcome: Retrace recent actions and ask whether a lost item was found.
target_phrases: Я как раз собиралась отнести их в бюро находок

sentences.text: После работы Нина вышла из трамвая на Невском проспекте и сразу спрятала руки в карманы.
sentences.translation: After work, Nina stepped off the tram on Nevsky Prospekt and immediately tucked her hands into her pockets.

sentences.text: Правый карман был пуст: серых шерстяных перчаток нигде не было.
sentences.translation: The right pocket was empty; her gray wool gloves were nowhere to be found.

sentences.text: Нина вспомнила, что до трамвая заходила в кафе и снимала перчатки у стойки.
sentences.translation: Nina remembered that before the tram she had stopped at a café and taken off her gloves at the counter.

sentences.text: Сначала она ехала обратно две остановки, потом шла по мокрому тротуару к кафе.
sentences.translation: First she rode back two stops, then walked along the wet pavement to the café.

sentences.text: По дороге Нина нашла в кармане чек, который всё ещё пах корицей.
sentences.translation: On the way, Nina found a receipt in her pocket that still smelled of cinnamon.

sentences.text: У стойки она спросила: «Кажется, я оставила здесь перчатки. Вы ничего не находили?»
sentences.translation: At the counter she asked, “I think I left my gloves here. Did you happen to find anything?”

sentences.text: Бариста достала серую пару из ящика: «Я как раз собиралась отнести их в бюро находок — рядом лежал ваш чек».
sentences.translation: The barista took a gray pair from a drawer. “I was just about to take them to lost property—your receipt was beside them.”

sentences.text: На улице Нина надела ещё влажные перчатки и крепче взялась за холодный поручень трамвая.
sentences.translation: Outside, Nina pulled on the still-damp gloves and held the cold tram rail more firmly.

vocabulary.translation: Did you happen to find anything?

vocabulary.surface: собиралась отнести их в бюро находок
vocabulary.translation: was about to take them to lost property

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: I think I left my umbrella
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Кажется, я оставила зонт.
Пришлось ехать обратно две остановки.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: did you happen to find any keys?
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Извините, вы ключи не находили?
Я как раз собиралась звонить.

language_notes.title: Retrace a route in sequence
language_notes.explanation: Ехала marks travel by vehicle; шла marks directed movement on foot.
language_notes.example: Сначала она ехала обратно две остановки, потом шла по мокрому тротуару к кафе
language_notes.example_translation: First she rode back two stops, then walked along the wet pavement to the café
language_notes.pattern: Сначала + past action, потом + past action
variants: Сначала я ехал на метро, потом шёл пешком
Сначала мы зашли в магазин, потом вернулись домой
Сначала она позвонила, потом поехала обратно

language_notes.title: Ask gently about a lost item
language_notes.explanation: The negative question is a conventional, less abrupt way to ask whether staff found something.
language_notes.example: Вы ничего не находили?
language_notes.example_translation: Did you happen to find anything?

comprehension_questions.prompt: What makes Nina suspect the café rather than the tram?
choices: She remembers removing the gloves at the counter
She sees gloves through the café window
comprehension_questions.explanation: Her memory of снимала перчатки у стойки gives her a concrete last location.

comprehension_questions.prompt: How could the barista identify Nina?
choices: Her name is on the receipt
Her photograph is in a glove
comprehension_questions.explanation: The receipt connects the customer’s name to the gray gloves left near the counter.

sentence_building.answer: Правый карман был пуст: серых шерстяных перчаток нигде не было.
sentence_building.translation: The right pocket was empty; her gray wool gloves were nowhere to be found.

sentence_building.answer: Бариста достала серую пару из ящика: «Я как раз собиралась отнести их в бюро находок — рядом лежал ваш чек».
sentence_building.translation: The barista took a gray pair from a drawer. “I was just about to take them to lost property—your receipt was beside them.”

title: Записка на плане музея
subtitle: The Note on the Gallery Map
summary: At a Moscow exhibition, Denis loses sight of his friend and finds one penciled instruction clipped to the gallery map.
setting_tags: A fictional exhibition beside Gorky Park in Moscow
communicative_outcome: Follow a written direction and explain where two people will meet.
target_phrases: Я буду ждать у большого окна

sentences.text: В субботу Денис и Ира пришли на выставку рядом с Парком Горького.
sentences.translation: On Saturday, Denis and Ira came to an exhibition beside Gorky Park.

sentences.text: У первой инсталляции собралась толпа, и друзья потеряли друг друга из виду.
sentences.translation: A crowd gathered around the first installation, and the friends lost sight of each other.

sentences.text: Телефон Дениса не ловил сеть, поэтому он вернулся к стойке с бесплатными планами музея.
sentences.translation: Denis had no phone signal, so he returned to the stand with free gallery maps.

sentences.text: К одному плану была прикреплена записка: «Сначала пройди до конца зала».
sentences.translation: A note was clipped to one map: “First, walk to the end of the gallery.”

sentences.text: Ниже Ира написала: «Потом поверни направо у синей стены. Я буду ждать у большого окна».
sentences.translation: Below it, Ira had written: “Then turn right at the blue wall. I’ll wait by the big window.”

sentences.text: Денис прошёл мимо трёх тёмных залов и нашёл синюю перегородку.
sentences.translation: Denis passed three dark galleries and found the blue partition.

sentences.text: У окна Ира смотрела на поздний свет над парком и держала два бумажных стакана.
sentences.translation: By the window, Ira watched the late light over the park, holding two paper cups.

sentences.text: «Я знала, что ты заметишь записку», — сказала она и протянула ему кофе.
sentences.translation: “I knew you’d notice the note,” she said, handing him a coffee.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: В толпе я потерял друга из виду.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: Walk to the end of the corridor
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Пройдите до конца коридора.
У лестницы поверните направо.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: I will wait by the entrance
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Я буду ждать у входа.

language_notes.title: Give two directions in order
language_notes.explanation: Пройди and поверни are informal singular imperatives because Ira is writing to a close friend.
language_notes.example: Сначала пройди до конца зала
language_notes.example_translation: First, walk to the end of the gallery
variants: Сначала открой карту, потом найди выход
Сначала пройди прямо, потом остановись у окна

language_notes.title: Set a meeting point
language_notes.explanation: У marks a position beside a landmark and governs the genitive case.
language_notes.example: Я буду ждать у большого окна
language_notes.example_translation: I’ll wait by the big window

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why does Ira use a paper note instead of sending a message?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Телефон не ловил сеть establishes the practical reason for the handwritten route.

comprehension_questions.prompt: Which visual landmark confirms Denis is following the right route?
comprehension_questions.explanation: The note names a синяя стена, and Denis later finds the matching синяя перегородка.

sentence_building.answer: У первой инсталляции собралась толпа, и друзья потеряли друг друга из виду.
sentence_building.translation: A crowd gathered around the first installation, and the friends lost sight of each other.

sentence_building.answer: У окна Ира смотрела на поздний свет над парком и держала два бумажных стакана.
sentence_building.translation: By the window, Ira watched the late light over the park, holding two paper cups.

title: Двенадцатое место, шестой вагон
subtitle: Seat Twelve, Carriage Six
summary: On a weekend train from Moscow to Yaroslavl, two identical seat numbers expose Misha’s mistake and an unexpected shared book.
setting_tags: A weekend train from Moscow to Yaroslavl
grammar_focus: Identifying the wrong item with не тот
communicative_outcome: Compare ticket details, acknowledge a mistake, and start a polite conversation.
target_phrases: Кажется, у нас одно и то же место
Я вошёл не в тот вагон

sentences.text: В субботу утром Миша сел на поезд из Москвы в Ярославль и нашёл двенадцатое место у окна.
sentences.translation: On Saturday morning, Misha boarded a train from Moscow to Yaroslavl and found seat twelve by the window.

sentences.text: Он убрал мокрый зонт наверх и открыл книгу с загнутыми уголками страниц.
sentences.translation: He put his wet umbrella overhead and opened a book with dog-eared pages.

sentences.text: Через минуту подошла девушка и показала билет: «Кажется, у нас одно и то же место».
sentences.translation: A minute later, a young woman arrived and showed her ticket. “It looks like we have the same seat.”

sentences.text: Они сравнили номера: место было одинаковым, но на билетах стояли разные вагоны.
sentences.translation: They compared the numbers: the seat was the same, but the tickets listed different carriages.

sentences.text: Миша посмотрел на табличку у двери и вздохнул: «Я вошёл не в тот вагон».
sentences.translation: Misha looked at the sign by the door and sighed. “I got into the wrong carriage.”

sentences.text: Перед уходом он заметил у девушки книгу, которую только что открыл сам.
sentences.translation: Before leaving, he noticed that the woman had the same book he had just opened.

sentences.text: «Вы тоже её читаете?» — спросил Миша, и девушка показала закладку почти на той же странице.
sentences.translation: “Are you reading it too?” Misha asked, and she showed him a bookmark almost at the same page.

sentences.text: Они договорились встретиться за кофе на вокзале в Ярославле и разошлись по своим вагонам.
sentences.translation: They agreed to meet for coffee at the station in Yaroslavl, then went to their separate carriages.

pre_reading_vocabulary.example: В билетах указано одно и то же место.
Кажется, это не тот вагон.

pre_reading_vocabulary.translation: let us compare the ticket numbers
pre_reading_vocabulary.example: Давайте сравним номера билетов.
Мы договорились встретиться у вокзала.

language_notes.title: Acknowledge the wrong choice
language_notes.explanation: Тот agrees with the noun in gender and case; after в with motion, вагон takes the accusative.
language_notes.example: Я вошёл не в тот вагон
language_notes.example_translation: I got into the wrong carriage
variants: Я сел не на тот автобус

language_notes.title: Add information about a noun
language_notes.explanation: Которую is feminine accusative because it refers to книгу and is the object of открыл.
language_notes.example: он заметил у девушки книгу, которую только что открыл сам
language_notes.example_translation: he noticed that the woman had the same book he had just opened

comprehension_questions.prompt: Why do both travelers appear to have seat twelve?
choices: Their tickets are for different carriages
One ticket has the wrong date
comprehension_questions.explanation: The seat number matches, but the carriage numbers differ; Misha then sees he entered не в тот вагон.

comprehension_questions.prompt: What turns the awkward seat check into a friendly plan?
choices: They are reading the same book
comprehension_questions.explanation: The matching book and nearly matching page create a reason to continue the conversation over coffee.

sentence_building.answer: Он убрал мокрый зонт наверх и открыл книгу с загнутыми уголками страниц.
sentence_building.translation: He put his wet umbrella overhead and opened a book with dog-eared pages.

sentence_building.answer: «Вы тоже её читаете?» — спросил Миша, и девушка показала закладку почти на той же странице.
sentence_building.translation: “Are you reading it too?” Misha asked, and she showed him a bookmark almost at the same page.
